categories.title: Greetings & Expressions
categories.description: Essential greetings, polite phrases, and common everyday expressions

words.example: Olá, como estás?
words.exampleTranslation: Hello, how are you?

words.example: Bom dia, senhora.
words.exampleTranslation: Good morning, madam.
words.proTip: In Portugal, 'bom dia' is used until lunch (around 1–2pm). After that, switch to 'boa tarde'.

words.example: Boa tarde a todos.
words.exampleTranslation: Good afternoon everyone.
words.proTip: In Portugal, switch to 'boa tarde' after lunch (around 1–2pm). Before lunch: 'bom dia.' After dark: 'boa noite.'

words.example: Boa noite, dorme bem.
words.exampleTranslation: Good night, sleep well.
words.proTip: Used both as 'good evening' (when arriving) and 'good night' (when leaving). Same phrase for both — context tells you which.

words.example: Adeus, até amanhã!
words.exampleTranslation: Goodbye, see you tomorrow!
words.proTip: 'Adeus' is more final than 'até logo.' Use 'até logo' or 'até amanhã' when you expect to see the person again soon.

words.example: Muito obrigado pela ajuda.
words.exampleTranslation: Thank you very much for the help.
words.proTip: Men say 'obrigado,' women say 'obrigada' — it literally means 'obliged.' This is one of the few words in Portuguese where the speaker's gender matters, not the listener's.

words.example: Um café, por favor.
words.exampleTranslation: A coffee, please.
words.proTip: Say 'por favor' or 'faz favor' — both work. To call a waiter: 'Faz favor!' or raise your hand. Never snap your fingers.

words.example: Desculpe, onde fica o metro?
words.exampleTranslation: Excuse me, where is the metro?
words.proTip: 'Desculpe' works both for getting attention ('Excuse me, where is...?') and for apologizing. To pass through a crowd, use 'com licença.'

words.example: Sim, eu quero.
words.exampleTranslation: Yes, I want it.

words.example: Não, obrigado.
words.exampleTranslation: No, thank you.

words.example: Talvez vá ao cinema.
words.exampleTranslation: Maybe I'll go to the cinema.

words.example: Claro que sim!
words.exampleTranslation: Of course!
words.proTip: 'Claro!' or 'Claro que sim!' = Of course! Also means 'clear' (o céu está claro = the sky is clear).

words.example: Com certeza, eu ajudo.
words.exampleTranslation: For sure, I'll help.

words.example: Com licença, posso passar?
words.exampleTranslation: Excuse me, may I pass?
words.proTip: 'Com licença' is for passing through. 'Desculpe' is for getting attention or apologizing. To call a waiter, say 'Faz favor!' — never snap your fingers.

words.example: Parabéns pelo aniversário!
words.exampleTranslation: Happy birthday!
words.proTip: For birthdays: 'Parabéns!' or 'Parabéns pelo aniversário!' Also used for congratulations ( exams, new job).

words.example: Saúde! — quando alguém espirra.
words.exampleTranslation: Bless you! — when someone sneezes.
words.proTip: Say 'Saúde!' when someone sneezes. When toasting drinks, Portuguese often say 'Saúde!' or 'Tim-tim!' (clink). The word also means 'health' as a noun.

words.example: Pois, tens razão.
words.exampleTranslation: Indeed, you're right.
words.proTip: 'Pois' is a very Portuguese filler word — it means 'indeed,' 'right,' or 'well' depending on context. Used when agreeing: 'Pois, tens razão.'

words.example: Que fixe! Adorei.
words.exampleTranslation: How cool! I loved it.
words.proTip: 'Fixe' is THE word for 'cool' in Portugal. 'Que fixe!' = How cool! 'Bué fixe' = Super cool. It's informal but used by all ages. Never say 'legal' for cool — that's Brazilian.

words.example: Pronto, já está.
words.exampleTranslation: Done, it's ready.
words.proTip: Multi-use word: 'Pronto!' = Done! / Okay! / Ready! Also used to wrap up: 'Pronto, vou embora' = Right, I'm going.

words.example: Olá, como estás?
words.exampleTranslation: Hello, how are you?
words.proTip: Use 'como estás?' with friends and family (informal). For formal situations, use 'como está?' (você form).

words.example: Tudo bem? Há quanto tempo!
words.exampleTranslation: How's it going? Long time no see!

words.example: Tudo bem, obrigado.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm fine, thank you.

words.example: Até logo, bom trabalho!
words.exampleTranslation: See you later, good work!
words.proTip: 'Até logo' = see you later (same day). 'Até já' = see you in a moment. 'Até amanhã' = see you tomorrow.

words.example: Até amanhã, dorme bem.
words.exampleTranslation: See you tomorrow, sleep well.
words.proTip: Common goodbye. 'Amanhã' = tomorrow. Respond with 'Até amanhã!' or 'Até lá!'

words.example: Vou ali, até já!
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going over there, see you in a sec!
words.proTip: 'Até já' means you'll see the person very soon (minutes). 'Até logo' is for later the same day.

words.example: De nada, foi um prazer.
words.exampleTranslation: You're welcome, it was a pleasure.
words.proTip: 'De nada' is the standard response to 'obrigado/obrigada.' 'Não há de quê' is a slightly more formal alternative.

words.example: Está bem, eu faço isso.
words.exampleTranslation: Okay, I'll do that.

words.example: Muito prazer, sou o Rui.
words.exampleTranslation: Nice to meet you, I'm Rui.
words.proTip: In Portugal, people typically shake hands when meeting for the first time. Say 'Muito prazer' and your name. The other person usually replies 'Igualmente' or 'Também.'

words.example: Bom fim de semana! Igualmente!
words.exampleTranslation: Good weekend! Likewise!
words.proTip: Reply to 'Bom fim de semana!' or 'Muito prazer' — 'Igualmente!' = Likewise! / Same to you!

words.example: Um café, faz favor.
words.exampleTranslation: A coffee, please.
words.proTip: To call a waiter in Portugal, say 'Faz favor!' or raise your hand slightly — never snap your fingers. 'Um café, faz favor' = A coffee, please.

words.example: A conta, se faz favor.
words.exampleTranslation: The bill, if you please.

words.example: Boa sorte no exame!
words.exampleTranslation: Good luck on the exam!
words.proTip: Say before exams, interviews, trips: 'Boa sorte!' Reply: 'Obrigado!' or 'Obrigada!'

words.example: Bom apetite a todos!
words.exampleTranslation: Enjoy your meal, everyone!
words.proTip: In Portugal, say 'Bom apetite!' or 'Bom proveito!' before starting a meal. It's polite and expected — don't start eating until someone says it or until everyone is served.

words.example: Não faz mal, acontece.
words.exampleTranslation: No worries, it happens.
words.proTip: Reassuring: 'Não faz mal' = No worries / It doesn't matter. Like 'de nada' but for apologies. 'Desculpa!' — 'Não faz mal.'

words.example: Como se chama? Eu chamo-me Ana.
words.exampleTranslation: What is your name? My name is Ana.

words.example: Chamo-me Pedro, muito prazer.
words.exampleTranslation: My name is Pedro, nice to meet you.

words.example: Tchau, até amanhã!
words.exampleTranslation: Bye, see you tomorrow!

words.example: Quem é aquela pessoa?
words.exampleTranslation: Who is that person?

words.example: O quê? Não ouvi.
words.exampleTranslation: What? I didn't hear.

words.example: Onde moras?
words.exampleTranslation: Where do you live?

words.example: Quando chegas?
words.exampleTranslation: When do you arrive?

words.example: Como se diz isto em português?
words.exampleTranslation: How do you say this in Portuguese?

words.example: Porquê? O que aconteceu?
words.exampleTranslation: Why? What happened?

words.example: Porque estou cansado.
words.exampleTranslation: Because I'm tired.

words.example: Qual é o teu nome?
words.exampleTranslation: What's your name?

words.example: Quanto custa?
words.exampleTranslation: How much does it cost?

words.example: Quantos anos tens?
words.exampleTranslation: How many years old are you?

words.example: A minha casa é pequena.
words.exampleTranslation: My house is small.

words.example: O teu carro é novo.
words.exampleTranslation: Your car is new.

words.example: A tua mãe é simpática.
words.exampleTranslation: Your mother is nice.

words.example: A sua encomenda chegou.
words.exampleTranslation: Your order has arrived.

words.example: A nossa casa fica no centro.
words.exampleTranslation: Our house is in the centre.

words.example: O carro dele é azul.
words.exampleTranslation: His car is blue.

words.example: Este café é bom.
words.exampleTranslation: This coffee is good.

words.example: Esse livro é teu?
words.exampleTranslation: Is that book yours?

words.example: Aquela igreja é antiga.
words.exampleTranslation: That church is old.

words.example: O que é isto?
words.exampleTranslation: What is this?

words.example: Isso é verdade.
words.exampleTranslation: That's true.

words.example: O que é aquilo?
words.exampleTranslation: What is that?

words.example: Alguém está à porta.
words.exampleTranslation: Someone is at the door.

words.example: Não há ninguém em casa.
words.exampleTranslation: There's nobody at home.

words.example: Queres algo para beber?
words.exampleTranslation: Do you want something to drink?

words.example: Não sei nada.
words.exampleTranslation: I don't know anything.

words.example: Tudo bem? Tudo ótimo!
words.exampleTranslation: All good? All great!

words.example: Todos os dias estudo português.
words.exampleTranslation: Every day I study Portuguese.

words.example: Cada pessoa é diferente.
words.exampleTranslation: Each person is different.

words.example: Quero outra cerveja.
words.exampleTranslation: I want another beer.

words.example: Estou muito cansado.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm very tired.

words.example: Falo pouco português.
words.exampleTranslation: I speak little Portuguese.

words.example: Está bastante frio.
words.exampleTranslation: It's quite cold.

words.example: Quero mais café.
words.exampleTranslation: I want more coffee.

words.example: Há menos pessoas hoje.
words.exampleTranslation: There are fewer people today.

words.example: Temos dinheiro suficiente.
words.exampleTranslation: We have enough money.

words.example: Isto é demais!
words.exampleTranslation: This is too much!

words.example: Vou com a minha amiga.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going with my friend.

words.example: Café sem açúcar, por favor.
words.exampleTranslation: Coffee without sugar, please.

words.example: Isto é para ti.
words.exampleTranslation: This is for you.

words.example: A farmácia fica entre o banco e o café.
words.exampleTranslation: The pharmacy is between the bank and the café.

words.example: Falamos sobre o futuro.
words.exampleTranslation: We talked about the future.

words.example: Durante as férias fui a Portugal.
words.exampleTranslation: During the holidays I went to Portugal.

words.example: Desculpe o incómodo, sabe onde fica a farmácia?
words.exampleTranslation: Sorry to bother you, do you know where the pharmacy is?
words.proTip: The polite opener for stopping a stranger in the street. Portugal spells «incómodo» with an acute accent.

words.example: Já te sentes melhor? Ainda bem!
words.exampleTranslation: You're feeling better already? That's good!
words.proTip: «Ainda bem que vieste» = «I'm glad you came». It has nothing to do with «still».

words.english: not at all; don't mention it
words.example: Obrigado pela ajuda! — Ora essa, não foi nada.
words.exampleTranslation: Thanks for the help! — Don't mention it, it was nothing.
words.proTip: Said in reply to thanks or an apology. With a different tone it can also mean «Well, really!» in indignation.

words.english: by the way; while we're at it
words.example: Já agora, sabes a que horas abre o mercado?
words.exampleTranslation: By the way, do you know what time the market opens?
words.proTip: Extremely common for tacking on an extra question or request: «Já agora, traga-me também um café.»

words.example: Tens a entrevista amanhã? Força!
words.exampleTranslation: You have the interview tomorrow? Go for it!
words.proTip: Used to encourage someone; «Força, Portugal!» is the football chant.

words.example: Estás com gripe? Então as melhoras!
words.exampleTranslation: You've got the flu? Get well soon, then!
words.proTip: The standard thing to say to anyone who's ill — short for «desejo-te as melhoras».

words.example: Soube do teu avô. Os meus pêsames.
words.exampleTranslation: I heard about your grandfather. My condolences.

words.example: Os meus sentimentos a toda a família.
words.exampleTranslation: My sympathies to the whole family.
words.proTip: In everyday speech this is softer and more common than «os meus pêsames», which can sound formal.

words.example: Aqui está a sua francesinha. Bom proveito!
words.exampleTranslation: Here's your francesinha. Enjoy!
words.proTip: You'll hear it when walking past people eating, or from a waiter — reply «Obrigado».

words.example: Sou a Marta, a nova vizinha. Prazer em conhecê-lo.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm Marta, the new neighbour. Pleased to meet you.
words.proTip: Use «conhecê-lo» for a man, «conhecê-la» for a woman. With friends, «Muito gosto» is simpler.

words.example: Até à próxima, e cumprimentos à família!
words.exampleTranslation: Until next time, and my regards to the family!
words.proTip: Emails often end with «Cumprimentos» or «Com os melhores cumprimentos» — the equivalent of «Kind regards».

words.example: Ajudas-me com a mudança? — Com todo o gosto!
words.exampleTranslation: Will you help me move? — With pleasure!
words.proTip: Note «todo o gosto» with the article — Portugal says «todo o dia», «todo o gosto».

words.example: Muito obrigada pela boleia. — Não tem de quê.
words.exampleTranslation: Thanks a lot for the lift. — Don't mention it.

words.example: Obrigado pela informação. — Disponha.
words.exampleTranslation: Thanks for the information. — You're welcome.
words.proTip: Typical of shop staff and service workers — it means «I'm at your disposal».

words.example: Muito gosto em conhecê-la. — O gosto é todo meu.
words.exampleTranslation: Very nice to meet you. — The pleasure is all mine.

words.example: Partes amanhã para Madrid? Boa viagem!
words.exampleTranslation: You leave for Madrid tomorrow? Have a good trip!

words.example: Bem-vindos a Lisboa! Espero que gostem da cidade.
words.exampleTranslation: Welcome to Lisbon! I hope you enjoy the city.
words.proTip: It agrees with the person: bem-vindo, bem-vinda, bem-vindos, bem-vindas.

words.english: have a good rest of the day; carry on well
words.example: Obrigado pelo café. Boa continuação!
words.exampleTranslation: Thanks for the coffee. Have a good rest of your day!

relatedWords.meaning: have a nice rest of the day

words.proTip: A very Portuguese goodbye when leaving someone in the middle of their day, meal or work.

words.example: Até segunda, e bom fim de semana!
words.exampleTranslation: See you Monday, and have a nice weekend!
words.proTip: The usual reply is «Igualmente!» or «Para ti também!».

words.example: Boas festas e um feliz ano novo!
words.exampleTranslation: Happy holidays and a happy new year!

words.example: Já vais para casa? Bom descanso!
words.exampleTranslation: Heading home already? Get some good rest!

words.example: Não podes vir ao jantar? Que pena!
words.exampleTranslation: You can't come to the dinner? What a pity!

words.example: Perdeste a carteira? Que chatice!
words.exampleTranslation: You lost your wallet? What a pain!
words.proTip: Informal but perfectly polite — the go-to reaction to someone's minor misfortune.

words.example: Deixa estar, eu lavo a loiça depois.
words.exampleTranslation: Never mind, I'll do the dishes later.
words.proTip: Formal version: «Deixe estar». Also used to refuse help or payment politely.

words.example: Não te preocupes, eu levo-te ao aeroporto.
words.exampleTranslation: Don't worry, I'll take you to the airport.
words.proTip: It's a negative command, so it uses the conjuntivo. Formal: «Não se preocupe».

words.example: Vais casar? Muitas felicidades aos dois!
words.exampleTranslation: You're getting married? All the best to you both!
words.proTip: Used for weddings, new jobs and big life events — also a common sign-off on birthday cards.

words.example: Levantem os copos: à nossa!
words.exampleTranslation: Raise your glasses: cheers!
words.proTip: «Saúde!» is the most common toast; «À nossa!» is a warmer, friendly alternative.

words.example: Foi ótimo ver-te. Até à próxima!
words.exampleTranslation: It was great to see you. Until next time!
words.proTip: Portugal says «até à próxima» with the «à»; Brazil drops it.

words.example: Obrigado por tudo, e até breve!
words.exampleTranslation: Thanks for everything, and see you soon!
words.proTip: Vaguer than «até já» (minutes) or «até logo» (later today): «até breve» means some time soon, no date set.

words.example: Pronto, tenho de ir. Fica bem!
words.exampleTranslation: Right, I have to go. Take care!

categories.title: Numbers & Time
categories.description: Counting, telling time, days of the week, and temporal expressions

words.example: Quero um bilhete.
words.exampleTranslation: I want one ticket.

words.example: Dois cafés, por favor.
words.exampleTranslation: Two coffees, please.

words.example: Tenho três irmãos.
words.exampleTranslation: I have three siblings.

words.example: São quatro horas.
words.exampleTranslation: It's four o'clock.

words.example: Cinco minutos, por favor.
words.exampleTranslation: Five minutes, please.

words.example: Custa dez euros.
words.exampleTranslation: It costs ten euros.

words.example: Tenho vinte anos.
words.exampleTranslation: I am twenty years old.

words.example: Cem gramas de queijo.
words.exampleTranslation: One hundred grams of cheese.

words.example: A renda é mil euros.
words.exampleTranslation: The rent is one thousand euros.

words.example: É o primeiro dia.
words.exampleTranslation: It's the first day.

words.example: Que horas são?
words.exampleTranslation: What time is it?
words.proTip: 'Que horas são?' = What time is it? Portugal uses both 12h and 24h time. For 'it's 3pm' say 'São três da tarde' or 'São quinze horas.' Always feminine: 'É uma hora' (it's 1 o'clock).

words.example: Espera um minuto.
words.exampleTranslation: Wait a minute.
words.proTip: 'Um minuto' = one minute, or 'wait a moment.' 'Espera um minuto' = Wait a minute. Often said when busy.

words.example: Hoje é segunda-feira.
words.exampleTranslation: Today is Monday.
words.proTip: Pronunciation: 'OH-zhuh' — the 'j' sounds like French 'j' or 's' in 'measure.' Not like English 'j'.

words.example: Amanhã vou ao médico.
words.exampleTranslation: Tomorrow I'm going to the doctor.

words.example: Ontem choveu muito.
words.exampleTranslation: Yesterday it rained a lot.

words.example: A próxima semana.
words.exampleTranslation: Next week.
words.proTip: 'A próxima semana' = next week. 'Semana que vem' = the coming week. 'Na semana passada' = last week.

words.example: Este mês é janeiro.
words.exampleTranslation: This month is January.
words.proTip: Pronunciation: 'MAYSH' — like 'mes' in 'mesmerize' but with a slight 'sh' at the end. Plural: 'meses.'

words.example: Feliz ano novo!
words.exampleTranslation: Happy new year!
words.proTip: 'Tenho vinte anos' = I am twenty years old. The word 'anos' (years) is masculine, unlike English where we say 'years old.'

words.example: De manhã tomo café.
words.exampleTranslation: In the morning I have coffee.
words.proTip: Feminine: 'a manhã.' 'De manhã' = in the morning. 'Esta manhã' = this morning. Note: 'manhã' vs 'amanhã' (tomorrow).

words.example: À tarde vou correr.
words.exampleTranslation: In the afternoon I go running.
words.proTip: 'Tarde' has two meanings: 'afternoon' (feminine noun) and 'late' (adverb). 'Cheguei tarde' = I arrived late. Different stress in speech.

words.example: À noite vejo televisão.
words.exampleTranslation: In the evening I watch television.
words.proTip: Feminine: 'a noite.' 'À noite' = at night / in the evening. 'Boa noite' = good evening / good night.

words.example: Vamos agora.
words.exampleTranslation: Let's go now.
words.proTip: A-goh-rah. Common: 'Agora não' = Not now. 'Agora mesmo' = Right now. 'Até agora' = Until now.

words.example: Falamos depois.
words.exampleTranslation: We'll talk later.
words.proTip: 'Depois' = later / after. 'Falamos depois' = We'll talk later. 'Depois do jantar' = After dinner.

words.example: Antes do jantar.
words.exampleTranslation: Before dinner.
words.proTip: 'Antes' = before. 'Antes de' + infinitive. 'Antes do jantar' = Before dinner. Opposite of 'depois.'

words.example: Ela chega sempre a horas.
words.exampleTranslation: She always arrives on time.
words.proTip: Sempre = always. 'Sempre' before the verb: 'Ela sempre chega tarde' = She always arrives late.

words.example: Nunca fui ao Brasil.
words.exampleTranslation: I've never been to Brazil.
words.proTip: 'Nunca' comes before the verb: 'Nunca fui' = I've never been. 'Não... nunca' = never (double negative is normal in Portuguese).

words.example: Às vezes como fora.
words.exampleTranslation: Sometimes I eat out.
words.proTip: Às vezes = sometimes. 'Às vezes como fora' = Sometimes I eat out. Note the 'às' (contraction).

words.example: Acordei cedo hoje.
words.exampleTranslation: I woke up early today.
words.proTip: 'Cedo' = early (adverb). 'De manhã cedo' = early in the morning. Don't confuse with 'cedo' in 'até logo' — different context.

words.example: Entretanto, podes preparar a mesa.
words.exampleTranslation: Meanwhile, you can set the table.

words.example: Antigamente não havia telemóveis.
words.exampleTranslation: In the old days there were no mobile phones.

words.example: Segunda-feira vou ao médico.
words.exampleTranslation: On Monday I'm going to the doctor.
words.proTip: Weekdays in Portugal: segunda, terça, quarta, quinta, sexta. All take 'feira' — from the old market days.

words.example: À terça-feira tenho aula de português.
words.exampleTranslation: On Tuesday I have Portuguese class.

words.example: Quarta-feira é dia de mercado.
words.exampleTranslation: Wednesday is market day.

words.example: Na quinta-feira janto fora.
words.exampleTranslation: On Thursday I have dinner out.

words.example: Sexta-feira saio mais cedo.
words.exampleTranslation: On Friday I leave earlier.

words.example: Ao sábado vou à praia.
words.exampleTranslation: On Saturday I go to the beach.
words.proTip: Sábado = Saturday. Masculine. 'Ao sábado' = on Saturday. Weekend starts here!

words.example: Ao domingo descanso em casa.
words.exampleTranslation: On Sunday I rest at home.
words.proTip: Domingo = Sunday. Traditional family day — almoço with parents/grandparents.

words.example: O que vais fazer no fim de semana?
words.exampleTranslation: What are you going to do at the weekend?
words.proTip: In Portugal, 'fim de semana' (literally 'end of week') is Saturday and Sunday. Say 'Bom fim de semana!' on Fridays.

words.example: Vou ao ginásio uma vez por semana.
words.exampleTranslation: I go to the gym once a week.

words.example: Tomo café duas vezes por dia.
words.exampleTranslation: I have coffee twice a day.

words.example: Esperei meia hora.
words.exampleTranslation: I waited half an hour.

words.example: Chego num quarto de hora.
words.exampleTranslation: I'll arrive in a quarter of an hour.

words.example: Chegámos de madrugada.
words.exampleTranslation: We arrived in the early hours.
words.proTip: 'De madrugada' = in the early hours (roughly 2–6am). Portuguese nightlife often goes 'até de madrugada' — until the small hours.

words.example: O almoço é ao meio-dia.
words.exampleTranslation: Lunch is at noon.
words.proTip: Meio-dia = noon. 'O almoço é ao meio-dia' — Portuguese lunch is often 12:30–2pm.

words.example: O filme acaba à meia-noite.
words.exampleTranslation: The film ends at midnight.
words.proTip: Meia-noite = midnight. 'À meia-noite' = at midnight. Feminine.

words.example: Anteontem fui ao dentista.
words.exampleTranslation: The day before yesterday I went to the dentist.

words.example: Vou viajar depois de amanhã.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm travelling the day after tomorrow.

words.example: Voltamos daqui a uma quinzena.
words.exampleTranslation: We'll be back in a fortnight.

words.example: O castelo é do século XV.
words.exampleTranslation: The castle is from the 15th century.

words.example: Amanhã é feriado.
words.exampleTranslation: Tomorrow is a public holiday.
words.proTip: Feriado = public holiday. Shops closed, families together. 'Amanhã é feriado.'

words.example: Desculpe, que horas são?
words.exampleTranslation: Excuse me, what time is it?
words.proTip: Portugal uses 24h time in writing. In speech: 'São três da tarde' or 'São quinze horas.' Always feminine: 'É uma hora.'

words.example: Tenho seis irmãos.
words.exampleTranslation: I have six siblings.

words.example: São sete horas da manhã.
words.exampleTranslation: It's seven in the morning.

words.example: Ela trabalha oito horas por dia.
words.exampleTranslation: She works eight hours a day.

words.example: A loja fecha às nove.
words.exampleTranslation: The shop closes at nine.

words.example: Temos onze jogadores na equipa.
words.exampleTranslation: We have eleven players on the team.

words.example: São doze meses no ano.
words.exampleTranslation: There are twelve months in the year.

words.example: Hoje é dia treze.
words.exampleTranslation: Today is the thirteenth.

words.example: O meu sobrinho tem catorze anos.
words.exampleTranslation: My nephew is fourteen years old.

words.example: Faltam quinze minutos.
words.exampleTranslation: Fifteen minutes left.

words.example: Ela começou a trabalhar aos dezasseis.
words.exampleTranslation: She started working at sixteen.

words.example: O autocarro chega às dezassete e trinta.
words.exampleTranslation: The bus arrives at seventeen thirty.

words.example: Aos dezoito anos já podia votar.
words.exampleTranslation: At eighteen he could already vote.

words.example: Dezanove pessoas vieram à festa.
words.exampleTranslation: Nineteen people came to the party.

words.example: Ela tem trinta anos.
words.exampleTranslation: She is thirty years old.

words.example: Quarenta alunos estão inscritos.
words.exampleTranslation: Forty students are enrolled.

words.example: O livro custa cinquenta euros.
words.exampleTranslation: The book costs fifty euros.

words.example: A avó tem sessenta e cinco anos.
words.exampleTranslation: Grandma is sixty-five years old.

words.example: Setenta por cento concordaram.
words.exampleTranslation: Seventy percent agreed.

words.example: O bisavô viveu até aos oitenta.
words.exampleTranslation: The great-grandfather lived to eighty.

words.example: Noventa dias são três meses.
words.exampleTranslation: Ninety days is three months.

words.example: O meu aniversário é em janeiro.
words.exampleTranslation: My birthday is in January.

words.example: Fevereiro é o mês mais curto.
words.exampleTranslation: February is the shortest month.

words.example: A primavera começa em março.
words.exampleTranslation: Spring starts in March.

words.example: Em abril, águas mil.
words.exampleTranslation: In April, a thousand rains.

words.example: O Dia da Mãe é em maio.
words.exampleTranslation: Mother's Day is in May.

words.example: As festas populares são em junho.
words.exampleTranslation: The popular festivals are in June.

words.example: Julho é o mês mais quente.
words.exampleTranslation: July is the hottest month.

words.example: Vamos de férias em agosto.
words.exampleTranslation: We go on holiday in August.

words.example: As aulas começam em setembro.
words.exampleTranslation: Classes start in September.

words.example: O outono começa em outubro.
words.exampleTranslation: Autumn starts in October.

words.example: Em novembro já chove muito.
words.exampleTranslation: In November it already rains a lot.

words.example: O Natal é em dezembro.
words.exampleTranslation: Christmas is in December.

words.example: Espera um segundo, por favor.
words.exampleTranslation: Wait a second, please.

words.example: Moro no terceiro andar.
words.exampleTranslation: I live on the third floor.

words.example: Este é o último dia de aulas.
words.exampleTranslation: This is the last day of school.

words.example: As contas da luz chegam uma vez por trimestre.
words.exampleTranslation: The electricity bills arrive once a quarter.

words.example: No segundo semestre tenho aulas à noite.
words.exampleTranslation: In the second semester I have evening classes.

words.example: De vez em quando vamos jantar a Alfama.
words.exampleTranslation: From time to time we go out to dinner in Alfama.

words.example: Ultimamente tenho dormido muito mal.
words.exampleTranslation: Lately I've been sleeping really badly.
words.proTip: Pairs naturally with the pretérito perfeito composto: «Ultimamente tenho trabalhado muito» = an ongoing, repeated situation.

words.example: O teu irmão ligou há pouco.
words.exampleTranslation: Your brother called a little while ago.

words.example: Espera, daqui a pouco já estou pronto.
words.exampleTranslation: Wait, I'll be ready in a little while.
words.proTip: «Daqui a» looks forward, «há» looks back: daqui a dois dias (in two days) vs há dois dias (two days ago).

words.example: Prefiro ir ao ginásio a meio da semana.
words.exampleTranslation: I prefer to go to the gym midweek.

relatedWords.meaning: in the middle of the month

words.example: Vamos ao Algarve no fim de semana prolongado.
words.exampleTranslation: We're going to the Algarve on the long weekend.

relatedWords.meaning: to take the bridge day off

words.proTip: When a holiday falls on a Tuesday or Thursday, many people «fazem ponte» and take the Monday or Friday off too.

words.example: Na véspera de Natal janta-se bacalhau.
words.exampleTranslation: On Christmas Eve people eat salt cod for dinner.

words.example: Dê-me meia dúzia de pastéis de nata, por favor.
words.exampleTranslation: Give me half a dozen custard tarts, please.
words.proTip: Eggs and pastéis de nata are often sold by the dúzia or meia dúzia; «meia dúzia de pessoas» also means just a handful of people.

words.example: A renda aqui custa o dobro do que pagava.
words.exampleTranslation: The rent here costs double what I used to pay.

words.example: Comi só metade da francesinha.
words.exampleTranslation: I only ate half of the francesinha.
words.proTip: Use «metade» for half of something (metade do bolo) and «meio/meia» before a noun (meia hora, meio quilo).

words.example: Um terço do ordenado vai para a renda.
words.exampleTranslation: A third of my salary goes on rent.

words.example: Os preços subiram cinco por cento este ano.
words.exampleTranslation: Prices went up five percent this year.

words.example: Vivo em Lisboa há quase uma década.
words.exampleTranslation: I've lived in Lisbon for almost a decade.

words.example: Convém marcar mesa com antecedência ao sábado.
words.exampleTranslation: It's best to book a table in advance on Saturdays.

words.example: Corri muito, mas cheguei a tempo ao comboio.
words.exampleTranslation: I ran a lot, but I got to the train in time.

words.example: Evita o metro à hora de ponta.
words.exampleTranslation: Avoid the metro at rush hour.

words.example: A cidade recebe milhões de turistas por ano.
words.exampleTranslation: The city receives millions of tourists a year.
words.proTip: In Portugal «bilião» means a million million (10¹²); a thousand million is «mil milhões».

words.example: A encomenda chega em três dias úteis.
words.exampleTranslation: The order arrives in three working days.

categories.title: Colours & Weather
categories.description: Colours, weather conditions, and seasonal vocabulary

words.example: O carro vermelho é meu.
words.exampleTranslation: The red car is mine.
words.proTip: Colour adjectives agree: 'carro vermelho' (m), 'casa vermelha' (f). In Portugal, red wine = vinho tinto.

words.example: O céu está azul.
words.exampleTranslation: The sky is blue.
words.proTip: Agrees with noun: 'céu azul,' 'camisa azul' (blue is invariable — ends in consonant).

words.example: Gosto de verde.
words.exampleTranslation: I like green.
words.proTip: Portuguese love verde — parks, countryside, 'verde' symbolises nature. 'Pôr a verde' = to criticise severely.

words.example: A banana é amarela.
words.exampleTranslation: The banana is yellow.
words.proTip: Amarelo (yellow) — the -o/-a agreement: 'sol amarelo,' 'casa amarela.'

words.example: Vinho branco, por favor.
words.exampleTranslation: White wine, please.
words.proTip: Vinho branco = white wine. 'Em branco' = blank. Branco (white) agrees: branco/branca.

words.example: Café preto, sem açúcar.
words.exampleTranslation: Black coffee, no sugar.
words.proTip: Café preto = black coffee (no milk). Preto agrees: preto/preta.

words.example: Ela tem olhos castanhos.
words.exampleTranslation: She has brown eyes.
words.proTip: Castanho = brown. Common for eyes: 'olhos castanhos.' Also chestnut — castanhas in autumn.

words.example: A camisa é cor-de-rosa.
words.exampleTranslation: The shirt is pink.
words.proTip: Invariable — doesn't change for gender: 'camisa cor-de-rosa,' 'casaco cor-de-rosa.'

words.example: As flores são roxas.
words.exampleTranslation: The flowers are purple.
words.proTip: Roxo (purple) — 'roxo' can also mean bruised: 'joelho roxo' = bruised knee.

words.example: O dia está cinzento.
words.exampleTranslation: The day is grey.
words.proTip: O dia está cinzento = The day is grey. Portuguese use this a lot for cloudy Lisbon weather.

words.example: Hoje está sol.
words.exampleTranslation: It's sunny today.
words.proTip: 'Está sol' = It's sunny. In Portugal the sun can be strong — say 'protector solar' for sunscreen.

words.example: Está a chover.
words.exampleTranslation: It's raining.
words.proTip: In Lisbon, rain can come suddenly. 'Está a chover' = It's raining. Always carry an 'guarda-chuva' in winter.

words.example: Está muito vento.
words.exampleTranslation: It's very windy.
words.proTip: Portugal's coast is windy — 'Está muito vento' = It's very windy. Norte (north wind) brings cold.

words.example: Está frio hoje.
words.exampleTranslation: It's cold today.
words.proTip: 'Está frio' = It's cold. Portuguese homes can feel cold in winter — heating isn't always central.

words.example: Está muito quente.
words.exampleTranslation: It's very hot.
words.proTip: 'Está quente' = It's hot (weather). 'A água está quente' = The water is hot. Quente is invariable.

words.example: O céu está cheio de nuvens.
words.exampleTranslation: The sky is full of clouds.
words.proTip: Feminine: a nuvem, nuvens. 'O céu está cheio de nuvens' = The sky is full of clouds.

words.example: Nunca neva em Lisboa.
words.exampleTranslation: It never snows in Lisbon.
words.proTip: Rare in Lisbon — 'Nunca neva aqui.' In Serra da Estrela they have snow. Feminine.

words.example: Há trovoada esta noite.
words.exampleTranslation: There's a thunderstorm tonight.
words.proTip: Trovoada = thunderstorm. 'Há trovoada' = There's a thunderstorm. Summer storms are common.

words.example: A temperatura é de 25 graus.
words.exampleTranslation: The temperature is 25 degrees.
words.proTip: Ask: 'Qual é a temperatura?' Portugal uses Celsius. 25° = 'vinte e cinco graus.'

words.example: A previsão do tempo diz que vai chover.
words.exampleTranslation: The weather forecast says it will rain.
words.proTip: Check 'previsão do tempo' on TV or IPMA.pt. Portuguese love talking about weather.

words.example: O pôr do sol está laranja.
words.exampleTranslation: The sunset is orange.
words.proTip: 'Laranja' = both the fruit (orange) and the colour. Same word in EP and BR.

words.example: A luz dourada da tarde.
words.exampleTranslation: The golden afternoon light.
words.proTip: Dourado = golden. 'Luz dourada' = golden light. Common for sunset descriptions.

words.example: O carro prateado é novo.
words.exampleTranslation: The silver car is new.
words.proTip: Prateado = silver. Often for cars: 'carro prateado.'

words.example: O azul escuro é bonito.
words.exampleTranslation: Dark blue is beautiful.
words.proTip: Verde escuro = dark green. Escuro agrees: escuro/escura.

words.example: Prefiro verde claro.
words.exampleTranslation: I prefer light green.
words.proTip: 'Claro' = light (colour) or 'of course!' Don't confuse: 'verde claro' = light green; 'Claro que sim!' = Of course!

words.example: Há muito nevoeiro de manhã.
words.exampleTranslation: There's a lot of fog in the morning.
words.proTip: Common in Lisbon mornings, especially near the river. 'Há muito nevoeiro' = There's a lot of fog.

words.example: Vem aí uma tempestade.
words.exampleTranslation: A storm is coming.
words.proTip: Tempestade = storm. 'Vem aí uma tempestade' = A storm is coming. Stay indoors.

words.example: Está só um chuvisco.
words.exampleTranslation: It's just a drizzle.
words.proTip: Chuvisco = drizzle. Portuguese drizzle (brisa) is typical — light rain, no umbrella needed sometimes.

words.example: Caiu granizo ontem.
words.exampleTranslation: It hailed yesterday.
words.proTip: Granizo = hail. Rare but happens. 'Caiu granizo' = It hailed.

words.example: A primavera começa em março.
words.exampleTranslation: Spring starts in March.
words.proTip: March–June. Best time to visit — flowers, mild weather. 'Na primavera' = in spring.

words.example: No verão vamos à praia.
words.exampleTranslation: In summer we go to the beach.
words.proTip: June–September. Hot and dry. 'No verão' = in summer. Beach season.

words.example: O outono é a minha estação preferida.
words.exampleTranslation: Autumn is my favourite season.
words.proTip: September–December. 'No outono' = in autumn. Castanhas (chestnuts) and vindima (grape harvest).

words.example: No inverno faz muito frio.
words.exampleTranslation: In winter it's very cold.
words.proTip: December–March. 'No inverno' = in winter. Rainy, cold, but rarely freezing in Lisbon.

words.example: Qual é a tua estação do ano preferida?
words.exampleTranslation: What is your favourite season?
words.proTip: As quatro estações = the four seasons. Primavera, verão, outono, inverno.

words.example: O clima em Lisboa é húmido.
words.exampleTranslation: The climate in Lisbon is humid.
words.proTip: Portugal spells it 'húmido' (with h), not 'úmido' — that's Brazilian. Lisbon's climate can be húmido, especially near the river.

words.example: Hoje está calor.
words.exampleTranslation: Today it's hot.
words.proTip: 'Está calor' (impersonal) = It's hot. Don't say 'eu estou calor' — wrong. 'Tenho calor' = I'm hot.

words.example: Está frio lá fora.
words.exampleTranslation: It's cold outside.
words.proTip: 'Está frio' = It's cold. 'Tenho frio' = I'm cold (personal). Portuguese homes can feel cold in winter.

words.example: Leva o guarda-chuva, está a chover.
words.exampleTranslation: Take the umbrella, it's raining.
words.proTip: Present continuous: estar a + infinitive. 'Está a chover' = It's raining. Very common structure in EP.

words.example: Onde está o meu guarda-chuva?
words.exampleTranslation: Where is my umbrella?
words.proTip: Literally 'rain guard.' Essential in Lisbon winters. 'Leva o guarda-chuva' = Take the umbrella.

words.example: Está bom tempo para um passeio.
words.exampleTranslation: The weather is nice for a walk.
words.proTip: 'Está bom tempo' = The weather is nice. Perfect for 'Vamos dar um passeio?' (Shall we go for a walk?).

words.example: Depois da chuva apareceu um arco-íris.
words.exampleTranslation: After the rain a rainbow appeared.

words.example: Há geada no vidro do carro.
words.exampleTranslation: There is frost on the car window.

words.example: Hoje está nublado.
words.exampleTranslation: It's cloudy today.

words.example: Está muito abafado hoje.
words.exampleTranslation: It's very muggy today.

words.example: De manhã está fresco.
words.exampleTranslation: It's cool in the morning.

words.example: O clima em Lisboa é ameno.
words.exampleTranslation: The climate in Lisbon is mild.

words.example: Há uma brisa agradável.
words.exampleTranslation: There's a pleasant breeze.

words.example: Vi um relâmpago ao longe.
words.exampleTranslation: I saw lightning in the distance.

words.example: O trovão assustou o cão.
words.exampleTranslation: The thunder scared the dog.

words.example: Este verão houve uma grande seca.
words.exampleTranslation: This summer there was a big drought.

words.example: As chuvas causaram inundações.
words.exampleTranslation: The rains caused floods.

words.example: Houve cheias no Algarve.
words.exampleTranslation: There was flooding in the Algarve.

words.example: Temos de proteger o ambiente.
words.exampleTranslation: We have to protect the environment.

words.example: Gosto de estar na natureza.
words.exampleTranslation: I like being in nature.

words.example: A poluição do ar é um problema.
words.exampleTranslation: Air pollution is a problem.

words.example: O clima em Portugal é bom.
words.exampleTranslation: The climate in Portugal is good.

words.example: Estamos a usar energia solar.
words.exampleTranslation: We're using solar energy.

words.example: O turismo sustentável é importante.
words.exampleTranslation: Sustainable tourism is important.

words.example: Prefiro produtos ecológicos.
words.exampleTranslation: I prefer eco-friendly products.

words.example: Compro legumes orgânicos no mercado.
words.exampleTranslation: I buy organic vegetables at the market.

words.example: Reduzam o uso de plástico.
words.exampleTranslation: Reduce the use of plastic.

words.example: O aquecimento global é real.
words.exampleTranslation: Global warming is real.

words.example: O IPMA emitiu aviso amarelo por causa da chuva.
words.exampleTranslation: IPMA issued a yellow warning because of the rain.
words.proTip: IPMA's scale goes verde, amarelo, laranja, vermelho. Check ipma.pt before hiking or going to the beach.

words.example: Há aviso laranja para a costa por causa da agitação marítima.
words.exampleTranslation: There's an orange warning for the coast because of rough seas.

words.example: Leva um casaco, que à noite está fresquinho.
words.exampleTranslation: Bring a jacket, it's chilly at night.
words.proTip: The diminutive softens it: «está fresquinho» is chilly but pleasant, never freezing.

words.example: A previsão é de aguaceiros durante a tarde.
words.exampleTranslation: The forecast is for showers in the afternoon.

words.example: Amanhã vamos ter céu limpo e muito sol.
words.exampleTranslation: Tomorrow we'll have clear skies and lots of sun.

words.example: De manhã o céu vai estar encoberto no litoral.
words.exampleTranslation: In the morning the sky will be overcast on the coast.

words.example: Esta onda de frio fez disparar a conta da luz.
words.exampleTranslation: This cold snap sent the electricity bill soaring.

words.example: Vai haver aguaceiros com algumas abertas à tarde.
words.exampleTranslation: There'll be showers with some sunny spells in the afternoon.

words.example: Na Costa da Caparica a nortada estragou o dia de praia.
words.exampleTranslation: At Costa da Caparica the north wind ruined the beach day.
words.proTip: The summer «nortada» is why Portuguese beachgoers carry windbreaks.

words.example: Uma rajada de vento levou-me o guarda-chuva.
words.exampleTranslation: A gust of wind took my umbrella.

words.example: O tempo vai continuar instável até ao fim de semana.
words.exampleTranslation: The weather will stay unsettled until the weekend.

words.example: Está um frio de rachar, nem consigo sentir os dedos.
words.exampleTranslation: It's freezing, I can't even feel my fingers.

words.example: É só chuva miudinha, mas molha muito.
words.exampleTranslation: It's only drizzle, but it gets you soaked.

words.example: De manhã a relva está cheia de orvalho.
words.exampleTranslation: In the morning the grass is covered in dew.

words.example: Para a entrevista, levo o fato azul-marinho.
words.exampleTranslation: For the interview, I'll wear the navy blue suit.

categories.title: Food & Drink
categories.description: Restaurants, grocery shopping, cooking, and common ingredients

words.example: Uma garrafa de água, por favor.
words.exampleTranslation: A bottle of water, please.
words.proTip: At restaurants, specify 'com gás' or 'sem gás' — otherwise you might get whichever they have. Tap water ('água da torneira') is safe to drink in Portugal but not always offered.

words.example: Quero um café com leite.
words.exampleTranslation: I want a coffee with milk.
words.proTip: In Lisbon, order a 'bica' for espresso. In Porto, say 'cimbalino.' A 'café' works everywhere. 'Um café, por favor' is probably the most useful sentence in Portugal.

words.example: Um chá de camomila.
words.exampleTranslation: A chamomile tea.

words.example: Bebo leite ao pequeno-almoço.
words.exampleTranslation: I drink milk at breakfast.

words.example: Sumo de laranja natural.
words.exampleTranslation: Fresh orange juice.
words.proTip: In Portugal it's 'sumo' (juice), not 'suco' (Brazilian). 'Sumo de laranja natural' = fresh orange juice.

words.example: Uma cerveja, faz favor.
words.exampleTranslation: A beer, please.
words.proTip: Order 'uma imperial' for a small draft beer (the standard size). 'Uma caneca' = a pint-sized mug.

words.example: Vinho tinto da casa.
words.exampleTranslation: House red wine.

words.example: Duas imperiais, por favor.
words.exampleTranslation: Two draught beers, please.

words.example: Pão fresco da padaria.
words.exampleTranslation: Fresh bread from the bakery.
words.proTip: Bread is sacred in Portugal. At restaurants, bread and olives ('couvert') often appear automatically — but they're not free! You can politely decline.

words.example: Queijo da Serra é delicioso.
words.exampleTranslation: Serra cheese is delicious.

words.example: Não como carne.
words.exampleTranslation: I don't eat meat.

words.example: Frango assado com batatas.
words.exampleTranslation: Roast chicken with potatoes.

words.example: Em Portugal comemos muito peixe.
words.exampleTranslation: In Portugal we eat a lot of fish.
words.proTip: Peixe = fish. Same singular/plural in some contexts. Portugal eats a lot of peixe — coastal nation.

words.example: O bacalhau à Brás é típico.
words.exampleTranslation: Bacalhau à Brás is typical.
words.proTip: Bacalhau (salt cod) is Portugal's national dish — there are hundreds of recipes. Always soaked before cooking to remove salt.

words.example: Arroz de marisco.
words.exampleTranslation: Seafood rice.

words.example: Batatas fritas ou cozidas?
words.exampleTranslation: Fried or boiled potatoes?

words.example: Dois ovos estrelados.
words.exampleTranslation: Two fried eggs.

words.example: Uma salada mista.
words.exampleTranslation: A mixed salad.

words.example: Sopa de legumes.
words.exampleTranslation: Vegetable soup.
words.proTip: Portuguese often start lunch with soup — 'sopa de legumes' or 'caldo verde' (kale soup). It's a staple.

words.example: Como fruta todos os dias.
words.exampleTranslation: I eat fruit every day.

words.example: A maçã é a minha fruta preferida.
words.exampleTranslation: The apple is my favourite fruit.

words.example: Laranjas do Algarve.
words.exampleTranslation: Oranges from the Algarve.
words.proTip: 'Laranja' = both the fruit (orange) and the colour. Same word in EP and BR.

words.example: Salada de tomate e cebola.
words.exampleTranslation: Tomato and onion salad.

words.example: Refoga a cebola em azeite.
words.exampleTranslation: Sauté the onion in olive oil.

words.example: Dois dentes de alho.
words.exampleTranslation: Two cloves of garlic.

words.example: Azeite português é o melhor.
words.exampleTranslation: Portuguese olive oil is the best.

words.example: Passa-me o sal.
words.exampleTranslation: Pass me the salt.

words.example: Sem açúcar, por favor.
words.exampleTranslation: Without sugar, please.
words.proTip: Order coffee: 'com açúcar' or 'sem açúcar.' Many Portuguese drink 'café sem açúcar' — bitter is the norm.

words.example: Pão com manteiga.
words.exampleTranslation: Bread with butter.

words.example: Uma tosta de presunto e queijo.
words.exampleTranslation: A toasted sandwich with ham and cheese.
words.proTip: Presunto = cured ham (like prosciutto). Fiambre = cooked ham for sandwiches. Presunto is a Portuguese delicacy.

words.example: Os pastéis de nata de Belém.
words.exampleTranslation: The custard tarts from Belém.
words.proTip: Portugal's iconic custard tart. Best warm with cinnamon. The original is from Belém — 'pastéis de Belém.'

words.example: Quer sobremesa?
words.exampleTranslation: Would you like dessert?

words.example: O pequeno-almoço está incluído.
words.exampleTranslation: Breakfast is included.
words.proTip: Always say 'pequeno-almoço' in Portugal, never 'café da manhã' (that's Brazilian). A typical Portuguese breakfast is a galão (milky coffee) with a tosta mista (toasted ham and cheese).

words.example: Vamos almoçar juntos?
words.exampleTranslation: Shall we have lunch together?
words.proTip: Portuguese lunch is usually 12:30–2pm. Many restaurants have 'prato do dia' (dish of the day) — cheap and good.

words.example: O jantar é às oito.
words.exampleTranslation: Dinner is at eight.

words.example: Hora do lanche!
words.exampleTranslation: Snack time!

words.example: Este restaurante é bom.
words.exampleTranslation: This restaurant is good.

words.example: Posso ver a ementa?
words.exampleTranslation: May I see the menu?
words.proTip: In Portugal it's 'ementa' or 'carta' for menu, not 'cardápio' (Brazilian). 'Posso ver a ementa?' = May I see the menu?

words.example: A conta, por favor.
words.exampleTranslation: The bill, please.
words.proTip: Say 'A conta, por favor' to ask for the bill. Tipping in Portugal is appreciated but not obligatory — rounding up or leaving 5-10% is common.

words.example: Preciso de um garfo.
words.exampleTranslation: I need a fork.

words.example: A faca não corta.
words.exampleTranslation: The knife doesn't cut.

words.example: Uma colher de sopa.
words.exampleTranslation: A soup spoon.

words.example: O prato do dia.
words.exampleTranslation: The dish of the day.

words.example: Um copo de água.
words.exampleTranslation: A glass of water.

words.example: Uma garrafa de vinho.
words.exampleTranslation: A bottle of wine.

words.example: Tem guardanapos?
words.exampleTranslation: Do you have napkins?

words.example: Gosto de cozinhar.
words.exampleTranslation: I like to cook.

words.example: Deixa a água ferver.
words.exampleTranslation: Let the water boil.

words.example: Vou assar o frango.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going to roast the chicken.

words.example: Não frites com muito óleo.
words.exampleTranslation: Don't fry with too much oil.

words.example: Tens a receita do bolo?
words.exampleTranslation: Do you have the cake recipe?

words.example: A comida está deliciosa.
words.exampleTranslation: The food is delicious.

words.example: Este piri-piri é muito picante.
words.exampleTranslation: This piri-piri is very spicy.
words.proTip: Portuguese love piri-piri (chilli sauce). 'Não é picante?' = Isn't it spicy? Chicken piri-piri is a classic.

words.example: A sopa está muito salgada.
words.exampleTranslation: The soup is too salty.

words.example: Este bolo é muito doce.
words.exampleTranslation: This cake is very sweet.

words.example: O café está amargo.
words.exampleTranslation: The coffee is bitter.

words.example: Vamos comer uns petiscos?
words.exampleTranslation: Shall we have some appetisers?
words.proTip: Petiscos = Portuguese tapas. Order a few with beer or wine at a tasca. 'Uma tasca' = a casual tavern.

words.example: Portugal tem marisco excelente.
words.exampleTranslation: Portugal has excellent seafood.
words.proTip: Portugal has excellent seafood. 'Arroz de marisco' and 'cataplana' are classics. Always ask 'está fresco?' = is it fresh?

words.example: Peixe grelhado com legumes.
words.exampleTranslation: Grilled fish with vegetables.

words.example: Compro pão na padaria.
words.exampleTranslation: I buy bread at the bakery.
words.proTip: Pastelaria = café + pastries. Padaria = bakery (mainly bread). Many places are both. Buy 'pão quente' in the morning.

words.example: Como legumes ao jantar.
words.exampleTranslation: I eat vegetables at dinner.

categories.title: Travel & Directions
categories.description: Transport, hotels, asking for help, and getting around

words.example: O aeroporto de Lisboa.
words.exampleTranslation: The Lisbon airport.
words.proTip: Lisbon airport is officially 'Aeroporto Humberto Delgado' but locals just say 'o aeroporto.' You'll hear 'porta de embarque' for boarding gate.

words.example: O avião parte às dez.
words.exampleTranslation: The plane departs at ten.

words.example: Apanhei o comboio para o Porto.
words.exampleTranslation: I caught the train to Porto.
words.proTip: 'Comboio' is European Portuguese — never say 'trem' (that's Brazilian). The CP (Comboios de Portugal) runs the national rail network.

words.example: O autocarro passa às nove.
words.exampleTranslation: The bus comes at nine.
words.proTip: 'Autocarro' is strictly PT-PT. In Brazil they say 'ônibus.' In Lisbon, use the Carris network; intercity buses are run by Rede Expressos.

words.example: A estação de metro é aqui perto.
words.exampleTranslation: The metro station is nearby.

words.example: Chamei um táxi.
words.exampleTranslation: I called a taxi.
words.proTip: Uber and Bolt work in Lisbon and Porto. Traditional táxis use meters. From the airport, agree on price or use the meter.

words.example: Vou de carro.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going by car.

words.example: Ando de bicicleta todos os dias.
words.exampleTranslation: I ride a bicycle every day.

words.example: Apanhamos o barco para Cacilhas.
words.exampleTranslation: We take the boat to Cacilhas.

words.example: O eléctrico 28 é famoso.
words.exampleTranslation: Tram 28 is famous.
words.proTip: The famous Eléctrico 28 runs through Lisbon's historic neighborhoods. Locals pronounce it 'eh-LEK-tree-koo' with the accent on the second syllable.

words.example: Onde compro o bilhete?
words.exampleTranslation: Where do I buy the ticket?
words.proTip: In Lisbon, most people use a 'Viva Viagem' rechargeable card rather than single bilhetes. 'Passe mensal' is the monthly pass.

words.example: Um bilhete de ida e volta.
words.exampleTranslation: A return ticket.
words.proTip: At the bilheteira (ticket office), say 'Um bilhete de ida e volta para...' for a return, or 'Só ida' for one-way.

words.example: A hora de partida é às seis.
words.exampleTranslation: The departure time is at six.

words.example: A chegada é ao meio-dia.
words.exampleTranslation: The arrival is at noon.

words.example: O comboio tem vinte minutos de atraso.
words.exampleTranslation: The train is twenty minutes late.
words.proTip: CP trains can have delays. 'O comboio tem atraso' = The train is delayed. Check cp.pt for updates.

words.example: Onde é a farmácia mais próxima?
words.exampleTranslation: Where is the nearest pharmacy?
words.proTip: Portuguese pharmacies (marked with a green cross) can advise on minor ailments without a doctor's visit. There's always a 'farmácia de serviço' open 24h in each area — check the posted schedule on any pharmacy door.

words.exampleTranslation: Security at the airport is strict.

words.example: Tens seguro de viagem?
words.exampleTranslation: Do you have travel insurance?

words.example: O alarme disparou.
words.exampleTranslation: The alarm went off.

words.example: O ladrão fugiu.
words.exampleTranslation: The thief ran away.

words.example: Alguém está ferido?
words.exampleTranslation: Is anyone injured?

words.example: A vítima está consciente.
words.exampleTranslation: The victim is conscious.

words.example: A saída de emergência é à esquerda.
words.exampleTranslation: The emergency exit is on the left.

words.example: O extintor está no corredor.
words.exampleTranslation: The fire extinguisher is in the corridor.

words.example: Sabes primeiros socorros?
words.exampleTranslation: Do you know first aid?

words.example: Fui à polícia apresentar queixa.
words.exampleTranslation: I went to the police to file a complaint.

words.example: Há alguma testemunha?
words.exampleTranslation: Are there any witnesses?

words.example: Por favor, preciso de ajuda.
words.exampleTranslation: Please, I need help.

words.example: Chamem a polícia, houve um roubo!
words.exampleTranslation: Call the police, there's been a robbery!

words.example: Chamem uma ambulância, há um ferido!
words.exampleTranslation: Call an ambulance, someone's injured!

words.example: Está bem? Precisa de ajuda?
words.exampleTranslation: Are you okay? Do you need help?

words.example: O número de emergência em Portugal é o 112.
words.exampleTranslation: The emergency number in Portugal is 112.

words.example: Uso o passe para apanhar o metro e o autocarro.
words.exampleTranslation: I use my travel pass to take the metro and the bus.
words.proTip: In Lisbon the Navegante pass covers metro, Carris, CP trains and ferries across the whole metro area for a flat monthly price.

words.english: to top up / renew the travel pass
words.example: Tenho de carregar o passe antes do dia um.
words.exampleTranslation: I have to top up my pass before the first of the month.

words.example: O revisor pediu-me o bilhete logo a seguir a Sintra.
words.exampleTranslation: The inspector asked for my ticket right after Sintra.
words.proTip: Fines for travelling without a validated ticket are steep, and «esqueci-me» rarely works with the revisor.

words.example: Com a Via Verde não precisas de parar nas portagens.
words.exampleTranslation: With Via Verde you don't need to stop at the tolls.
words.proTip: Via Verde also pays for many car parks and some petrol stations. Rental cars usually offer it for a small daily fee.

words.example: Por causa das obras, há um desvio na Avenida da Liberdade.
words.exampleTranslation: Because of the roadworks, there's a diversion on Avenida da Liberdade.

words.example: Apanhei um engarrafamento enorme na Ponte 25 de Abril.
words.exampleTranslation: I got stuck in a huge traffic jam on the 25 de Abril bridge.
words.proTip: On the radio you'll also hear «trânsito condicionado» for slow or restricted traffic.

words.example: Se não te despachas, vamos perder o comboio.
words.exampleTranslation: If you don't hurry up, we'll miss the train.

words.example: O comboio para o Porto parte do cais número cinco.
words.exampleTranslation: The train to Porto leaves from platform five.

relatedWords.meaning: a Lisbon station by the river

words.proTip: Stations show «linha» for the track number; «cais» is the platform itself and also the riverside quay.

words.example: Só levo bagagem de mão para não pagar mais.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm only taking hand luggage so I don't pay extra.

words.example: Tens o cartão de embarque no telemóvel?
words.exampleTranslation: Do you have the boarding pass on your phone?

words.example: O voo para Luanda tem escala em Lisboa.
words.exampleTranslation: The flight to Luanda has a stopover in Lisbon.

words.example: Para conhecer o Alentejo, o melhor é alugar um carro.
words.exampleTranslation: To see the Alentejo, the best thing is to rent a car.
words.proTip: Use «alugar» for cars and flats alike; «arrendar» is only for long-term property rental.

words.example: Não te esqueças de validar o bilhete à entrada.
words.exampleTranslation: Don't forget to validate your ticket when you get on.

words.example: Para ir a Belém, fazes transbordo no Cais do Sodré.
words.exampleTranslation: To get to Belém, you change at Cais do Sodré.

words.example: Temos de parar na próxima bomba de gasolina.
words.exampleTranslation: We need to stop at the next petrol station.
words.proTip: «Atestar» means to fill the tank right up: «Atesta, se faz favor.»

words.example: É impossível estacionar em Alfama ao fim de semana.
words.exampleTranslation: It's impossible to park in Alfama at the weekend.

words.example: A porta de embarque mudou para a quarenta e dois.
words.exampleTranslation: The boarding gate changed to forty-two.

words.example: Parámos numa estação de serviço para tomar um café.
words.exampleTranslation: We stopped at a service station for a coffee.

words.example: Não podes virar aqui, essa rua é de sentido único.
words.exampleTranslation: You can't turn here, that street is one-way.

words.example: Podes dar-me boleia até à estação?
words.exampleTranslation: Can you give me a lift to the station?

relatedWords.meaning: to ask for a lift / hitchhike

words.proTip: Brazilians say «dar carona»; in Portugal it's always «boleia».

categories.title: Home & Rooms
categories.description: Types of housing, rooms, furniture, appliances, and household items

words.example: A minha casa é pequena.
words.exampleTranslation: My house is small.
words.proTip: 'Em casa' = at home (no article). 'Na casa' = in the house (specific). 'Estou em casa' = I'm home.

words.example: Moro num apartamento.
words.exampleTranslation: I live in an apartment.

words.example: A cozinha é grande.
words.exampleTranslation: The kitchen is big.

words.example: Estamos na sala.
words.exampleTranslation: We're in the living room.
words.proTip: Sala = living room. 'Sala de estar' = sitting room. Central to Portuguese homes — where guests sit.

words.example: O quarto tem uma janela grande.
words.exampleTranslation: The bedroom has a big window.

words.example: Onde é a casa de banho?
words.exampleTranslation: Where is the bathroom?
words.proTip: In Portugal it's always 'casa de banho,' never 'banheiro' (that's Brazilian and sounds odd in Portugal). In a restaurant, ask 'Onde é a casa de banho?'

words.example: Tomo café na varanda.
words.exampleTranslation: I have coffee on the balcony.
words.proTip: Varanda = balcony. Many Lisbon flats have one. 'Tomar café na varanda' = have coffee on the balcony.

words.example: Temos um jardim pequeno.
words.exampleTranslation: We have a small garden.

words.example: O carro está na garagem.
words.exampleTranslation: The car is in the garage.

words.example: Sobe as escadas.
words.exampleTranslation: Go up the stairs.
words.proTip: Escadas = stairs. Feminine plural. 'Moro no 3º andar' = I live on 3rd floor — no elevator in old buildings.

words.example: A cama é confortável.
words.exampleTranslation: The bed is comfortable.

words.example: Põe a mesa para o jantar.
words.exampleTranslation: Set the table for dinner.

words.example: Senta-te na cadeira.
words.exampleTranslation: Sit on the chair.

words.example: Vou sentar-me no sofá.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going to sit on the sofa.

words.example: A roupa está no armário.
words.exampleTranslation: The clothes are in the wardrobe.

words.example: Olha-te ao espelho.
words.exampleTranslation: Look at yourself in the mirror.

words.example: Estou a ver televisão.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm watching television.

words.example: Esqueci o telemóvel em casa.
words.exampleTranslation: I forgot my phone at home.
words.proTip: 'Telemóvel' is PT-PT — never say 'celular' (that's Brazilian). From 'tele' (distant) + 'móvel' (mobile). Portugal's main operators are MEO, NOS, and Vodafone.

words.example: Onde estão as chaves?
words.exampleTranslation: Where are the keys?

words.example: Fecha a porta.
words.exampleTranslation: Close the door.
words.proTip: Porta = door. 'Bater à porta' = to knock on the door. 'Porta aberta' = open door (welcoming).

words.example: Abre a janela.
words.exampleTranslation: Open the window.
words.proTip: Janela = window. 'Abrir a janela' = open the window. Portuguese love fresh air.

words.example: Apaga a luz.
words.exampleTranslation: Turn off the light.

words.example: Passa o aspirador na sala.
words.exampleTranslation: Vacuum the living room.

words.example: Põe a máquina de lavar a trabalhar.
words.exampleTranslation: Put the washing machine on.

words.example: O leite está no frigorífico.
words.exampleTranslation: The milk is in the fridge.

words.example: Cuidado com o fogão.
words.exampleTranslation: Be careful with the stove.
words.proTip: Fogão = stove. Many Portuguese cook on gas (gás). 'Cuidado com o fogão' = careful with the stove.

words.example: A renda é cara em Lisboa.
words.exampleTranslation: The rent is expensive in Lisbon.
words.proTip: Renda = rent (the payment). 'A renda é cara em Lisboa' = Rent is expensive in Lisbon. Pay 'no início do mês' = at the start of the month.

words.example: A mudança é no sábado.
words.exampleTranslation: The move is on Saturday.

words.example: As caixas estão no sótão.
words.exampleTranslation: The boxes are in the attic.

words.example: O vinho está na cave.
words.exampleTranslation: The wine is in the cellar.
words.proTip: Cave = basement or wine cellar. Portuguese often keep wine 'na cave.'

words.example: Moro no terceiro andar.
words.exampleTranslation: I live on the third floor.

words.example: A vizinhança é tranquila.
words.exampleTranslation: The neighbourhood is quiet.
words.proTip: Vizinhança = neighbourhood. Portuguese often know their neighbours — community matters.

words.example: Preciso de uma panela grande.
words.exampleTranslation: I need a big pot.

words.example: Frita o ovo na frigideira.
words.exampleTranslation: Fry the egg in the frying pan.

words.example: Põe no forno a 180 graus.
words.exampleTranslation: Put it in the oven at 180 degrees.

words.example: Aquece no micro-ondas.
words.exampleTranslation: Heat it in the microwave.
words.proTip: Micro-ondas = microwave. 'Aquecer no micro-ondas' = heat in the microwave.

words.example: A loiça está no lava-loiça.
words.exampleTranslation: The dishes are in the sink.

words.example: Os talheres estão na gaveta.
words.exampleTranslation: The cutlery is in the drawer.

words.example: Os copos estão na prateleira.
words.exampleTranslation: The glasses are on the shelf.

words.example: Onde estão os talheres?
words.exampleTranslation: Where is the cutlery?

words.example: Põe a toalha de mesa.
words.exampleTranslation: Put the tablecloth on.

words.example: Usa o avental para cozinhar.
words.exampleTranslation: Wear the apron for cooking.

words.example: Passa-me uma toalha.
words.exampleTranslation: Pass me a towel.

words.example: O sabonete está ao lado do lavatório.
words.exampleTranslation: The soap is next to the sink.

words.example: Preciso de comprar champô.
words.exampleTranslation: I need to buy shampoo.

words.example: Onde está a minha escova de dentes?
words.exampleTranslation: Where is my toothbrush?

words.example: A pasta de dentes acabou.
words.exampleTranslation: The toothpaste ran out.

words.example: Vou tomar um duche rápido.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going to take a quick shower.
words.proTip: In Portugal: 'tomar banho' = to have a shower/bath. 'Vou tomar um duche' = I'm going to take a shower. Never 'tomar uma ducha' (Brazilian).

words.example: A casa de banho tem banheira.
words.exampleTranslation: The bathroom has a bathtub.

words.example: Lava as mãos no lavatório.
words.exampleTranslation: Wash your hands at the sink.

words.example: O secador de cabelo está na gaveta.
words.exampleTranslation: The hair dryer is in the drawer.

words.example: Preciso de duas almofadas.
words.exampleTranslation: I need two pillows.

words.example: No inverno uso um cobertor.
words.exampleTranslation: In winter I use a blanket.

words.example: Mudei os lençóis hoje.
words.exampleTranslation: I changed the sheets today.

words.example: O colchão é novo.
words.exampleTranslation: The mattress is new.

words.example: O livro está na mesinha de cabeceira.
words.exampleTranslation: The book is on the bedside table.

words.example: Acende o candeeiro.
words.exampleTranslation: Turn on the lamp.
words.proTip: Candeeiro = lamp. 'Acender o candeeiro' = turn on the lamp. Portuguese use candeeiros, not just ceiling lights.

words.example: Fecha as cortinas.
words.exampleTranslation: Close the curtains.

words.example: O despertador toca às sete.
words.exampleTranslation: The alarm goes off at seven.
words.proTip: Despertador = alarm clock. 'O despertador toca às sete' = The alarm goes off at seven.

words.example: O tapete é novo.
words.exampleTranslation: The rug is new.

words.example: Os livros estão na estante.
words.exampleTranslation: The books are on the bookshelf.

words.example: Onde está o comando da televisão?
words.exampleTranslation: Where is the TV remote?

words.example: O quadro na parede é bonito.
words.exampleTranslation: The painting on the wall is beautiful.

words.example: Acende a lareira, está frio.
words.exampleTranslation: Light the fireplace, it's cold.

words.example: O meu vizinho é muito simpático.
words.exampleTranslation: My neighbour is very friendly.

words.example: A renda é paga no início do mês.
words.exampleTranslation: The rent is paid at the start of the month.

words.example: Vamos mudar de casa no próximo mês.
words.exampleTranslation: We're moving house next month.

words.example: O chão da cozinha é de azulejo.
words.exampleTranslation: The kitchen floor is tiled.

words.example: O teto é muito alto.
words.exampleTranslation: The ceiling is very high.

words.example: Vou pintar a parede de branco.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going to paint the wall white.

words.example: O interruptor está ao lado da porta.
words.exampleTranslation: The light switch is next to the door.

words.example: Onde é a tomada para o carregador?
words.exampleTranslation: Where's the socket for the charger?

words.example: Vou varrer a cozinha com a vassoura.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going to sweep the kitchen with the broom.

words.example: Podes levar o lixo lá fora?
words.exampleTranslation: Can you take the rubbish out?

words.example: Alguém tocou a campainha.
words.exampleTranslation: Someone rang the doorbell.

words.example: Vou aspirar a sala.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going to vacuum the living room.

words.example: Preciso de varrer a cozinha.
words.exampleTranslation: I need to sweep the kitchen.

words.example: Quem lava a loiça hoje?
words.exampleTranslation: Who's washing the dishes today?

words.example: Tenho de lavar roupa amanhã.
words.exampleTranslation: I have to do laundry tomorrow.

words.example: Vou estender a roupa na varanda.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going to hang the laundry on the balcony.

words.example: A roupa está a secar ao sol.
words.exampleTranslation: The clothes are drying in the sun.

words.example: Compra detergente no supermercado.
words.exampleTranslation: Buy detergent at the supermarket.

words.example: Passa a esfregona na cozinha.
words.exampleTranslation: Mop the kitchen floor.

words.example: Enche o balde com água.
words.exampleTranslation: Fill the bucket with water.

words.example: Limpa a mesa com um pano.
words.exampleTranslation: Wipe the table with a cloth.

words.example: A esponja está suja.
words.exampleTranslation: The sponge is dirty.

words.example: A reciclagem é importante.
words.exampleTranslation: Recycling is important.

words.example: Em Portugal reciclamos o vidro, papel e plástico.
words.exampleTranslation: In Portugal we recycle glass, paper, and plastic.

words.example: O contentor amarelo é para embalagens.
words.exampleTranslation: The yellow bin is for packaging.

words.example: Rega as plantas todos os dias.
words.exampleTranslation: Water the plants every day.

words.example: Vai à despensa buscar uma lata de atum.
words.exampleTranslation: Go to the pantry and get a tin of tuna.
words.proTip: Don't mix it up with 'dispensar' (to do without) — despensa is the food cupboard or small store room off the kitchen.

words.example: Agarra-te ao corrimão, que as escadas são íngremes.
words.exampleTranslation: Hold on to the handrail, the stairs are steep.

words.example: O autoclismo não para de correr.
words.exampleTranslation: The toilet cistern keeps running.
words.proTip: To flush is 'puxar o autoclismo' (or 'carregar no autoclismo' with a button). 'Descarga' is the Brazilian word.

words.example: A canalização deste prédio é muito antiga.
words.exampleTranslation: The plumbing in this building is very old.

words.example: O apartamento tem soalho de madeira em todas as divisões.
words.exampleTranslation: The flat has wooden floors in every room.
words.proTip: Old Lisbon flats often have original 'soalho' — lovely, but it creaks and carries noise to the neighbours below.

words.example: A lâmpada da cozinha está fundida, tenho de a trocar.
words.exampleTranslation: The kitchen bulb has blown, I need to change it.

words.example: A caldeira do aquecimento central avariou outra vez.
words.exampleTranslation: The central heating boiler broke down again.

words.example: Põe os pratos na máquina da loiça, por favor.
words.exampleTranslation: Put the plates in the dishwasher, please.
words.proTip: Everyday Portuguese for dishwasher; the full name 'máquina de lavar loiça' appears in shops and adverts.

words.example: Ao sábado limpo o pó dos móveis.
words.exampleTranslation: On Saturdays I dust the furniture.

words.example: O caixote do lixo está cheio, podes despejá-lo?
words.exampleTranslation: The bin is full, can you empty it?
words.proTip: Indoors it's the caixote do lixo; the big street bins are 'contentores'. Bin bags go down after 8 p.m. in many Lisbon areas.

words.example: O ferro de engomar está na despensa.
words.exampleTranslation: The iron is in the pantry.

words.example: Montei a tábua de engomar na sala.
words.exampleTranslation: I set up the ironing board in the living room.

words.example: Enquanto vejo televisão, dobro a roupa.
words.exampleTranslation: While I watch TV, I fold the laundry.

words.example: O vento levou a toalha porque faltavam molas.
words.exampleTranslation: The wind took the towel because there weren't enough pegs.

words.example: Põe as meias no cesto da roupa suja.
words.exampleTranslation: Put the socks in the laundry basket.

words.example: Lavo a casa de banho com lixívia.
words.exampleTranslation: I clean the bathroom with bleach.
words.proTip: Portuguese homes use lixívia for almost everything; never mix it with other cleaning products.

words.example: A sanita está entupida, temos de chamar o canalizador.
words.exampleTranslation: The toilet is blocked, we have to call the plumber.
words.proTip: The object is 'a sanita'; the room is 'a casa de banho'. Don't ask for 'a sanita' when you want the toilets in a café.

words.example: Trocámos a banheira por uma base de duche.
words.exampleTranslation: We swapped the bathtub for a shower tray.

words.example: O quarto tem um roupeiro embutido.
words.exampleTranslation: The bedroom has a built-in wardrobe.
words.proTip: In flat listings, 'roupeiro embutido' means built-in wardrobes — a real plus, since many old flats have none.

words.example: No inverno durmo com um edredão grosso.
words.exampleTranslation: In winter I sleep with a thick duvet.

words.example: Deixei o telemóvel na mesa de cabeceira.
words.exampleTranslation: I left my phone on the bedside table.

words.example: Guardo as camisolas na cómoda.
words.exampleTranslation: I keep my jumpers in the chest of drawers.
words.proTip: False friend: 'cómoda' is furniture, not a toilet. The adjective 'cómodo' means comfortable/convenient.

words.example: Liga o exaustor, que a cozinha está cheia de fumo.
words.exampleTranslation: Turn on the extractor fan, the kitchen is full of smoke.

words.example: A cozinha tem placa de indução e forno.
words.exampleTranslation: The kitchen has an induction hob and an oven.

words.example: Preciso de uma extensão para ligar o computador.
words.exampleTranslation: I need an extension lead to plug in the computer.

words.example: O puxador da gaveta partiu-se.
words.exampleTranslation: The drawer handle broke.

words.example: Há uma telha partida e o telhado mete água.
words.exampleTranslation: There's a broken tile and the roof lets in water.

words.example: Deixaram as bicicletas no patamar.
words.exampleTranslation: They left the bikes on the landing.

words.example: Cuidado com o degrau à entrada.
words.exampleTranslation: Mind the step at the entrance.

words.example: Pus a roupa a secar em cima do radiador.
words.exampleTranslation: I put the clothes to dry on the radiator.
words.proTip: Most Portuguese homes have no central heating; people rely on portable 'aquecedores a óleo' instead.

words.example: Usei água a ferver para desentupir o lava-loiça.
words.exampleTranslation: I used boiling water to unblock the sink.

words.example: A torneira da cozinha está sempre a pingar.
words.exampleTranslation: The kitchen tap is always dripping.

words.example: Lá em casa dividimos as tarefas domésticas.
words.exampleTranslation: At home we split the household chores.

words.example: A mulher a dias vem cá às sextas-feiras.
words.exampleTranslation: The cleaning lady comes on Fridays.
words.proTip: Very common in Portugal, usually paid by the hour. 'Empregada de limpeza' is the more neutral term.

words.example: Deixa os sapatos no hall de entrada.
words.exampleTranslation: Leave your shoes in the entrance hall.

words.example: Tive de esfregar o fogão durante meia hora.
words.exampleTranslation: I had to scrub the cooker for half an hour.

words.example: O ralo do duche está cheio de cabelos.
words.exampleTranslation: The shower drain is full of hair.

words.example: Quando os meus pais vêm, ficam no quarto de hóspedes.
words.exampleTranslation: When my parents come, they stay in the guest room.

words.example: No inverno uso a máquina de secar porque a roupa não seca.
words.exampleTranslation: In winter I use the tumble dryer because the washing won't dry.

words.example: Se quiseres, podes dormir no sofá-cama.
words.exampleTranslation: If you like, you can sleep on the sofa bed.

categories.title: Family & Daily Routine
categories.description: Family members, relationships, and everyday routines

words.example: A minha mãe chama-se Ana.
words.exampleTranslation: My mother is called Ana.
words.proTip: Mãe = mother. 'A minha mãe' — mãe is feminine. In Portugal, family names: mother's surname often comes last.

words.example: O meu pai é professor.
words.exampleTranslation: My father is a teacher.
words.proTip: Pai = father. Portuguese fathers traditionally had authority; modern families are more equal.

words.example: Os meus pais vivem no Porto.
words.exampleTranslation: My parents live in Porto.
words.proTip: Pais = parents (plural of pai in this sense). 'Os meus pais' = my parents. Don't confuse with país (country).

words.example: A minha filha tem cinco anos.
words.exampleTranslation: My daughter is five years old.
words.proTip: Filho/filha = son/daughter. 'Tenho um filho' = I have a son. Used for children of any age.

words.example: Tenho um irmão mais velho.
words.exampleTranslation: I have an older brother.
words.proTip: Irmão/irmã = brother/sister. 'Meus irmãos' can mean brothers or siblings (mixed).

words.example: A minha avó faz o melhor bolo.
words.exampleTranslation: My grandmother makes the best cake.
words.proTip: Avó (grandmother) vs avô (grandfather) — the accent changes the sound. Avó = ah-VOH, avô = ah-VAW. Easy to mix up!

words.example: O meu tio vive em Coimbra.
words.exampleTranslation: My uncle lives in Coimbra.
words.proTip: Tio/tia = uncle/aunt. Portuguese families are often close — 'almoço de família' on Sundays.

words.example: A minha prima casa em junho.
words.exampleTranslation: My cousin is getting married in June.
words.proTip: Primo/prima = cousin. 'Primos em segundo grau' = second cousins.

words.example: O meu marido é holandês.
words.exampleTranslation: My husband is Dutch.
words.proTip: Marido = husband. 'O meu marido' — common in all contexts.

words.example: A minha mulher é portuguesa.
words.exampleTranslation: My wife is Portuguese.
words.proTip: 'Mulher' = woman or wife. 'A minha mulher' = my wife. 'Esposa' is more formal. Both are used in Portugal.

words.example: A minha namorada é de Lisboa.
words.exampleTranslation: My girlfriend is from Lisbon.
