words.proTip: Namorado/namorada = boyfriend/girlfriend. More serious than 'amigo' — implies romantic relationship.

words.example: Vou sair com os meus amigos.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going out with my friends.
words.proTip: Amigo/amiga = friend. Portuguese value friendship deeply. 'Os meus amigos' = my friends.

words.example: Os vizinhos são simpáticos.
words.exampleTranslation: The neighbours are friendly.

words.example: Acordo às sete da manhã.
words.exampleTranslation: I wake up at seven in the morning.
words.proTip: Acordar = to wake up. 'Acordo às sete' = I wake up at seven. Reflexive optional in EP.

words.example: Levanto-me cedo.
words.exampleTranslation: I get up early.
words.proTip: Levantar-se = to get up. 'Levanto-me cedo' = I get up early. The 'me' is the reflexive pronoun.

words.example: Tomo banho de manhã.
words.exampleTranslation: I shower in the morning.
words.proTip: Tomar banho = to have a shower/bath. Never 'tomar uma ducha' (Brazilian). 'Tomei banho' = I showered.

words.example: Visto-me depressa.
words.exampleTranslation: I get dressed quickly.
words.proTip: Vestir-se = to get dressed. 'Visto-me depressa' = I get dressed quickly.

words.example: Saio de casa às oito.
words.exampleTranslation: I leave the house at eight.
words.proTip: Sair de casa = to leave the house. 'Saio de casa às oito' = I leave at eight.

words.example: Trabalho em casa.
words.exampleTranslation: I work from home.
words.proTip: Trabalhar = to work. 'Trabalho em casa' = I work from home. Portuguese work long hours by EU standards.

words.example: Preciso de descansar.
words.exampleTranslation: I need to rest.
words.proTip: Descansar = to rest. 'Preciso de descansar' = I need to rest. Sunday is often family rest day.

words.example: Durmo oito horas por noite.
words.exampleTranslation: I sleep eight hours a night.
words.proTip: Dormir = to sleep. Irregular: durmo, dormes, dorme. 'Durmo oito horas' = I sleep eight hours.

words.example: Deito-me à meia-noite.
words.exampleTranslation: I go to bed at midnight.
words.proTip: Deitar-se = to go to bed. 'Deito-me à meia-noite' = I go to bed at midnight.

words.example: Vou limpar a casa.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going to clean the house.
words.proTip: Limpar = to clean. 'Limpar a casa' = to clean the house. Saturday morning is often limpeza day.

words.example: Quem cozinha hoje?
words.exampleTranslation: Who's cooking today?

words.example: Vou lavar a roupa.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going to wash the clothes.
words.proTip: Lavar = to wash. 'Lavar a loiça' = wash the dishes. 'Lavar a roupa' = do the laundry.

words.example: Arruma o teu quarto.
words.exampleTranslation: Tidy up your room.
words.proTip: Arrumar = to tidy. 'Arruma o teu quarto!' = Tidy your room! (parent to child).

words.example: O meu sobrinho fez dois anos.
words.exampleTranslation: My nephew turned two.

words.example: A minha sogra cozinha muito bem.
words.exampleTranslation: My mother-in-law cooks very well.

words.example: O meu cunhado é do Porto.
words.exampleTranslation: My brother-in-law is from Porto.

words.example: O meu padrinho deu-me um relógio.
words.exampleTranslation: My godfather gave me a watch.

words.example: A avó tem cinco netos.
words.exampleTranslation: Grandma has five grandchildren.

words.example: Ela tem uma enteada de dez anos.
words.exampleTranslation: She has a ten-year-old stepdaughter.
words.proTip: Enteado/enteada = stepson/stepdaughter. Blended families use this. 'O meu enteado' = my stepson.

words.example: Ele é solteiro.
words.exampleTranslation: He is single.

words.example: Sou casado há cinco anos.
words.exampleTranslation: I've been married for five years.

words.example: Ela é divorciada.
words.exampleTranslation: She is divorced.

words.example: Penteio-me em frente ao espelho.
words.exampleTranslation: I comb my hair in front of the mirror.
words.proTip: Pentear-se = to comb one's hair. 'Penteio-me' = I comb my hair.

words.example: Barbeio-me todas as manhãs.
words.exampleTranslation: I shave every morning.
words.proTip: Barbear-se = to shave. 'Barbeio-me' = I shave. Or use 'fazer a barba.'

words.example: Ela maquilha-se rapidamente.
words.exampleTranslation: She puts on makeup quickly.

words.example: Faço a cama todos os dias.
words.exampleTranslation: I make the bed every day.
words.proTip: Fazer a cama = to make the bed. 'Faço a cama todos os dias' = I make the bed every day.

words.example: Podes pôr a mesa?
words.exampleTranslation: Can you set the table?
words.proTip: Pôr a mesa = to set the table. 'Põe a mesa para o jantar' = Set the table for dinner.

words.example: Quem levanta a mesa hoje?
words.exampleTranslation: Who's clearing the table today?
words.proTip: Levantar a mesa = to clear the table. Often followed by 'lavar a loiça.'

words.example: Odeio passar a ferro.
words.exampleTranslation: I hate ironing.
words.proTip: Passar a ferro = to iron. 'Passar a ferro a roupa' — Portuguese often iron everything, even jeans.

words.example: Desculpa, estou atrasada.
words.exampleTranslation: Sorry, I'm late.
words.proTip: Men say 'atrasado,' women 'atrasada' — the adjective agrees with the speaker. 'Desculpa, estou atrasada!' is common.

words.example: Tenho muito sono, vou dormir.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm very sleepy, I'm going to sleep.
words.proTip: Tenho sono = I'm sleepy. Different from 'estou cansado' (tired). 'Tenho' + noun for states.

words.example: O que vais fazer no fim de semana?
words.exampleTranslation: What are you going to do at the weekend?
words.proTip: Fim de semana = weekend. 'O que vais fazer no fim de semana?' — common Friday question.

words.example: Na segunda-feira é feriado.
words.exampleTranslation: Monday is a public holiday.
words.proTip: Feriado = public holiday. Portugal has ~13. Shops may be closed. 'É feriado amanhã.'

words.example: As coisas melhoram dia a dia.
words.exampleTranslation: Things get better day by day.
words.proTip: Dia a dia = day to day, daily. 'Vivo dia a dia' = I live day to day.

words.example: O bebé está a dormir.
words.exampleTranslation: The baby is sleeping.

words.example: A criança brinca no parque.
words.exampleTranslation: The child plays in the park.

words.example: Os adultos pagam preço inteiro.
words.exampleTranslation: Adults pay full price.

words.example: O idoso atravessou a rua devagar.
words.exampleTranslation: The elderly man crossed the street slowly.

words.example: A gravidez dela corre muito bem.
words.exampleTranslation: Her pregnancy is going very well.

words.example: A data de nascimento está no passaporte.
words.exampleTranslation: The date of birth is on the passport.

words.example: O casamento é em junho.
words.exampleTranslation: The wedding is in June.

words.example: O funeral foi muito emotivo.
words.exampleTranslation: The funeral was very emotional.

words.example: Tomo o pequeno-almoço às oito.
words.exampleTranslation: I have breakfast at eight.

words.example: Almoçamos juntos na cantina.
words.exampleTranslation: We have lunch together in the canteen.

words.example: Gosto de passear à beira-mar.
words.exampleTranslation: I like to go for a walk by the sea.

words.example: O meu pai conduz todos os dias.
words.exampleTranslation: My father drives every day.

words.example: Vou fazer compras ao supermercado.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going shopping at the supermarket.

words.example: O meu genro ajuda-me sempre com o computador.
words.exampleTranslation: My son-in-law always helps me with the computer.

words.example: A minha nora é enfermeira em Coimbra.
words.exampleTranslation: My daughter-in-law is a nurse in Coimbra.

words.example: Dou-me muito bem com o meu padrasto.
words.exampleTranslation: I get on really well with my stepfather.

words.example: A madrasta dela mora connosco há dez anos.
words.exampleTranslation: Her stepmother has lived with us for ten years.

words.example: Tenho um meio-irmão que vive no Porto.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a half-brother who lives in Porto.

words.example: Comprei uma bicicleta ao meu afilhado.
words.exampleTranslation: I bought my godson a bike.
words.proTip: Godparents matter in Portugal: the padrinho/madrinha traditionally gives the folar to their afilhado at Easter.

words.example: Casámo-nos numa quinta perto de Sintra.
words.exampleTranslation: We got married at a country estate near Sintra.
words.proTip: Both «casar» and «casar-se» are used; note the EP past «casámos» (with accent) vs the present «casamos».

words.example: Os pais dele divorciaram-se quando ele era pequeno.
words.exampleTranslation: His parents got divorced when he was little.

words.example: Foi a minha avó que me criou.
words.exampleTranslation: It was my grandmother who raised me.

words.example: Com os miúdos, a rotina da manhã é uma correria.
words.exampleTranslation: With the kids, the morning routine is a mad rush.

words.example: Ela cuida da mãe, que já tem noventa anos.
words.exampleTranslation: She looks after her mother, who's already ninety.

relatedWords.meaning: to take care of / deal with

words.example: Podes tomar conta do cão no fim de semana?
words.exampleTranslation: Can you look after the dog at the weekend?
words.proTip: «Tomar conta» is the everyday choice for babysitting or minding something short-term; «cuidar» feels more ongoing and caring.

words.example: Deixo o bebé na creche às oito.
words.exampleTranslation: I drop the baby off at nursery at eight.
words.proTip: Creche places in Lisbon are scarce: many parents sign up during the pregnancy. Creche Feliz makes many places free.

words.example: A nossa filha entra no infantário em setembro.
words.exampleTranslation: Our daughter starts kindergarten in September.

words.example: O divórcio foi difícil, mas já passou.
words.exampleTranslation: The divorce was hard, but it's over now.

words.example: Fomos aos Açores em lua de mel.
words.exampleTranslation: We went to the Azores on our honeymoon.

words.example: O vizinho de baixo é viúvo e vive sozinho.
words.exampleTranslation: The downstairs neighbour is a widower and lives alone.

words.example: No prédio mora um casal de reformados ingleses.
words.exampleTranslation: A couple of retired English people live in the building.

words.example: Separaram-se depois de quinze anos juntos.
words.exampleTranslation: They split up after fifteen years together.

words.example: A minha irmã engravidou do segundo filho.
words.exampleTranslation: My sister got pregnant with her second child.

words.example: Ele vai tirar um mês de licença parental.
words.exampleTranslation: He's going to take a month of parental leave.
words.proTip: Portugal's licença parental is shared between both parents, and part of the father's leave is compulsory.

words.example: No Natal juntam-se os parentes todos em casa da avó.
words.exampleTranslation: At Christmas all the relatives get together at Grandma's.
words.proTip: False friend: «os parentes» are relatives in general, not parents; parents are «os pais».

words.example: Em Portugal a família alargada ainda é muito próxima.
words.exampleTranslation: In Portugal the extended family is still very close.

words.example: Hoje sou eu que vou buscar os miúdos à escola.
words.exampleTranslation: Today I'm the one picking the kids up from school.
words.proTip: «Ir buscar» = go and fetch; «levar» = take somewhere. Vou levar os miúdos à escola e depois vou buscá-los.

words.example: Os miúdos estão a brincar no jardim.
words.exampleTranslation: The kids are playing in the garden.

categories.title: Work & Education
categories.description: Office, school, professions, and workplace vocabulary

words.example: O meu professor de português é simpático.
words.exampleTranslation: My Portuguese teacher is friendly.
words.proTip: Professor/professora = teacher. University teachers are also 'professor.' Very respected profession.

words.example: Preciso de ir ao médico.
words.exampleTranslation: I need to go to the doctor.
words.proTip: In Portugal, go to 'centro de saúde' for GP. For emergency: 'urgências' at hospital. Private: 'clínica.'

words.example: O advogado aconselhou-me.
words.exampleTranslation: The lawyer advised me.

words.example: A minha irmã é engenheira.
words.exampleTranslation: My sister is an engineer.

words.example: A enfermeira tomou a tensão.
words.exampleTranslation: The nurse took my blood pressure.

words.example: Chamei a polícia.
words.exampleTranslation: I called the police.

words.example: O cozinheiro fez um prato excelente.
words.exampleTranslation: The chef made an excellent dish.

words.example: Ela é jornalista num jornal.
words.exampleTranslation: She is a journalist at a newspaper.

words.example: O vendedor ajudou-me a escolher.
words.exampleTranslation: The salesperson helped me choose.

words.example: Os bombeiros apagaram o fogo.
words.exampleTranslation: The firefighters put out the fire.

words.example: Chamei o canalizador para a fuga.
words.exampleTranslation: I called the plumber for the leak.

words.example: O electricista reparou a instalação.
words.exampleTranslation: The electrician fixed the wiring.

words.example: O empregado de mesa trouxe a ementa.
words.exampleTranslation: The waiter brought the menu.
words.proTip: In Portugal: 'empregado de mesa' or 'empregado' — never 'garçom' (Brazilian). To call: 'Faz favor!' or raise your hand.

words.example: Ela é uma escritora conhecida.
words.exampleTranslation: She is a well-known writer.

words.example: O motorista do autocarro foi simpático.
words.exampleTranslation: The bus driver was friendly.

words.example: Trabalho num escritório no centro.
words.exampleTranslation: I work in an office in the centre.
words.proTip: 'Escritório' is the physical office. 'Trabalho' is work in general. 'Vou para o escritório' (I'm going to the office) vs 'Vou trabalhar' (I'm going to work).

words.example: A empresa tem cinquenta trabalhadores.
words.exampleTranslation: The company has fifty employees.
words.proTip: Empresa = company. 'Trabalhar numa empresa' = to work for a company. PME = small/medium enterprise.

words.example: Tenho uma reunião às dez.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a meeting at ten.
words.proTip: Reunião = meeting. 'Tenho uma reunião' = I have a meeting. Often long in Portugal!

words.example: O computador está avariado.
words.exampleTranslation: The computer is broken.
words.proTip: Computador = computer. 'Portátil' = laptop. Portuguese workplaces are increasingly digital.

words.example: O ecrã do portátil é grande.
words.exampleTranslation: The laptop screen is big.

words.example: O teclado está em português.
words.exampleTranslation: The keyboard is in Portuguese.

words.example: A impressora não tem tinta.
words.exampleTranslation: The printer has no ink.

words.example: Enviei-te um email.
words.exampleTranslation: I sent you an email.
words.proTip: Email = email. Pronounced 'ee-MAYL.' 'Enviei-te um email' = I sent you an email.

words.example: O correio eletrónico está cheio.
words.exampleTranslation: The email inbox is full.

words.example: Os meus colegas são simpáticos.
words.exampleTranslation: My colleagues are friendly.
words.proTip: Colega = colleague. Same for m/f! 'Os meus colegas' = my colleagues. Important in work culture.

words.example: O meu chefe aprovou o projeto.
words.exampleTranslation: My boss approved the project.
words.proTip: Chefe = boss. Same for m/f. 'O meu chefe' or 'A minha chefe.' Formal hierarchy in many companies.

words.example: O salário é pago no fim do mês.
words.exampleTranslation: The salary is paid at the end of the month.

words.example: Assinei o contrato de trabalho.
words.exampleTranslation: I signed the employment contract.

words.example: Tenho uma entrevista de emprego amanhã.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a job interview tomorrow.

words.example: Enviei o meu currículo.
words.exampleTranslation: I sent my CV.

words.example: Qual é o teu horário de trabalho?
words.exampleTranslation: What is your work schedule?

words.example: Os miúdos vão à escola de autocarro.
words.exampleTranslation: The children go to school by bus.
words.proTip: In Portugal: 'escola' = school; 'universidade' = university. Kids go to escola, adults to universidade or 'faculdade' (faculty).

words.example: Estudei na Universidade de Lisboa.
words.exampleTranslation: I studied at the University of Lisbon.
words.proTip: Universidade = university. Free for EU citizens in public unis. Lisbon, Porto, Coimbra are top.

words.example: A aula de português é às três.
words.exampleTranslation: The Portuguese class is at three.
words.proTip: Aula = class/lesson. 'A aula de português' = the Portuguese class. 'Ter aulas' = to have classes.

words.example: Tenho um exame na sexta-feira.
words.exampleTranslation: I have an exam on Friday.
words.proTip: Exame = exam. 'Fazer um exame' = to sit an exam. 'Boa sorte no exame!'

words.example: Sou aluno de português.
words.exampleTranslation: I am a Portuguese student.
words.proTip: Aluno/aluna = student. 'Sou aluno de português' = I'm a Portuguese student.

words.example: Comprei um livro novo.
words.exampleTranslation: I bought a new book.
words.proTip: Livro = book. 'Ler um livro' = to read a book. Livraria = bookshop (different from biblioteca).

words.example: Escrevo as notas no caderno.
words.exampleTranslation: I write the notes in the notebook.
words.proTip: Caderno = notebook. Students use cadernos. 'Escrever no caderno' = to write in the notebook.

words.example: Tens uma caneta para mim?
words.exampleTranslation: Do you have a pen for me?
words.proTip: Caneta = pen. 'Tens uma caneta?' = Do you have a pen? Caneta de feltro = marker.

words.example: Preciso de um lápis.
words.exampleTranslation: I need a pencil.

words.example: A mochila está na sala.
words.exampleTranslation: The backpack is in the living room.

words.example: Vou à biblioteca estudar.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going to the library to study.
words.proTip: Biblioteca = library. Free to use. 'Estudar na biblioteca' = to study at the library.

words.example: Consulta o dicionário.
words.exampleTranslation: Look it up in the dictionary.

words.example: Fiz um curso de português.
words.exampleTranslation: I did a Portuguese course.
words.proTip: Curso = course. 'Fiz um curso de português' = I did a Portuguese course. Curso intensivo = intensive.

words.example: Tive boa nota no exame.
words.exampleTranslation: I got a good grade in the exam.

words.example: Já fiz o trabalho de casa.
words.exampleTranslation: I've already done my homework.
words.proTip: Literally 'house work' — homework. 'Já fiz o trabalho de casa?' = Have you done your homework?

words.example: No recreio jogamos à bola.
words.exampleTranslation: At break we play ball.

words.example: O professor escreveu no quadro.
words.exampleTranslation: The teacher wrote on the blackboard.

words.example: Não posso falar, estou a trabalhar.
words.exampleTranslation: I can't talk, I'm working.

words.example: Fiz um estágio numa empresa.
words.exampleTranslation: I did an internship at a company.

words.example: O patrão quer falar contigo.
words.exampleTranslation: The boss wants to talk to you.
words.proTip: Patrão/patroa = boss (informal). More colloquial than chefe. 'O patrão não gostou.'

words.example: Foi despedido na semana passada.
words.exampleTranslation: He was fired last week.

words.example: Amanhã tenho folga.
words.exampleTranslation: I have the day off tomorrow.
words.proTip: Folga = day off. 'Tenho folga amanhã' = I have the day off tomorrow. 'Dia de folga.'

words.example: Nas férias fui ao Algarve.
words.exampleTranslation: On holiday I went to the Algarve.

words.example: O meu pai está na reforma.
words.exampleTranslation: My father is retired.
words.proTip: Reforma = retirement. 'Estar na reforma' = to be retired. Portuguese retire around 66.

words.example: O estagiário começa na segunda-feira.
words.exampleTranslation: The intern starts on Monday.

words.example: Estou desempregado há três meses.
words.exampleTranslation: I've been unemployed for three months.

words.example: Os meus pais já estão reformados.
words.exampleTranslation: My parents are already retired.

words.example: A empresa oferece formação gratuita.
words.exampleTranslation: The company offers free training.

words.example: Vou fazer uma pausa para café.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going to take a coffee break.

words.example: Ela estuda na faculdade de direito.
words.exampleTranslation: She studies at the law faculty.

words.example: Tenho uma licenciatura em engenharia.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a degree in engineering.

words.example: Está a fazer o mestrado em Lisboa.
words.exampleTranslation: He's doing his master's in Lisbon.

words.example: Enviei a candidatura pelo site da empresa.
words.exampleTranslation: I sent the application through the company's website.

words.example: Candidatei-me a três vagas esta semana.
words.exampleTranslation: I applied for three vacancies this week.
words.proTip: Use «candidatar-se a»: candidatar-se a um emprego, a uma bolsa, a um mestrado.

words.example: Tenho um contrato a termo de seis meses.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a six-month fixed-term contract.

words.example: Finalmente passei a contrato sem termo.
words.exampleTranslation: I finally got moved onto a permanent contract.
words.proTip: Landlords and banks often ask whether you have a contrato sem termo before renting or lending.

words.example: Trabalho a recibos verdes há dois anos.
words.exampleTranslation: I've been working as a freelancer for two years.
words.proTip: «Estar a recibos verdes» means working self-employed; receipts are now issued online on the Portal das Finanças.

words.example: Ainda estou no período experimental.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm still on my probation period.

words.example: Tenho direito a vinte e dois dias de férias pagas.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm entitled to twenty-two days of paid holiday.

words.example: O subsídio de férias costuma vir em junho.
words.exampleTranslation: The holiday bonus usually comes in June.
words.proTip: In Portugal salaries are paid 14 times a year: 12 months plus the subsídio de férias and the subsídio de Natal.

words.example: Com o subsídio de Natal pago as prendas.
words.exampleTranslation: I pay for the presents with my Christmas bonus.

words.example: Estive de baixa médica uma semana.
words.exampleTranslation: I was on sick leave for a week.
words.proTip: You don't call in «sick» casually: for more than a few days you need the baixa from a doctor, sent to the Segurança Social.

words.example: A chefia ainda não aprovou as minhas férias.
words.exampleTranslation: Management still hasn't approved my holidays.

words.example: Consegui uma bolsa de estudo para o mestrado.
words.exampleTranslation: I got a scholarship for my master's.

words.example: O ordenado cai na conta no dia vinte e cinco.
words.exampleTranslation: My pay goes into my account on the 25th.

words.example: Fiz horas extraordinárias para acabar o projeto.
words.exampleTranslation: I did overtime to finish the project.

words.example: Faço teletrabalho às segundas e sextas.
words.exampleTranslation: I work from home on Mondays and Fridays.

words.example: Vou pedir um aumento ao meu chefe.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going to ask my boss for a raise.

words.example: Há uma vaga para rececionista no hotel.
words.exampleTranslation: There's an opening for a receptionist at the hotel.

words.example: Esta semana estou no turno da noite.
words.exampleTranslation: This week I'm on the night shift.

words.example: Houve despedimentos na fábrica este mês.
words.exampleTranslation: There were layoffs at the factory this month.

words.example: Junta uma carta de apresentação ao currículo.
words.exampleTranslation: Attach a cover letter to your CV.

words.example: Chumbei no exame de condução à primeira vez.
words.exampleTranslation: I failed my driving test the first time.

categories.title: Health & Body
categories.description: Body parts, health, symptoms, and medical vocabulary

words.example: Dói-me a cabeça.
words.exampleTranslation: My head hurts.
words.proTip: Cabeça = head. Feminine: a cabeça. 'Dói-me a cabeça' = My head hurts (lit. It hurts me the head).

words.example: Tenho os olhos castanhos.
words.exampleTranslation: I have brown eyes.
words.proTip: Olho (eye) → olhos (eyes). Irregular plural! 'Tenho os olhos castanhos' = I have brown eyes.

words.example: O nariz está entupido.
words.exampleTranslation: My nose is blocked.
words.proTip: Nariz = nose. One nose, same form. 'O nariz está entupido' = My nose is blocked.

words.example: Abre a boca.
words.exampleTranslation: Open your mouth.
words.proTip: Boca = mouth. Feminine. 'Abre a boca' = Open your mouth (doctor/dentist).

words.example: Dói-me a orelha.
words.exampleTranslation: My ear hurts.
words.proTip: Orelha = ear. 'Dói-me a orelha' = My ear hurts. Orelha can also mean ear (of corn).

words.example: Tenho uma dor de dentes.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a toothache.
words.proTip: Dente → dentes (tooth/teeth). 'Dor de dentes' = toothache. Dentista = dentist.

words.example: O cabelo está molhado.
words.exampleTranslation: My hair is wet.
words.proTip: Cabelo = hair (as a whole). Usually singular: 'o cabelo.' 'O cabelo está molhado.'

words.example: Lava as mãos.
words.exampleTranslation: Wash your hands.
words.proTip: Mão (hand) → mãos (hands). Irregular! The only -ão word that becomes -ãos.

words.example: Parti o braço.
words.exampleTranslation: I broke my arm.
words.proTip: Braço → braços. 'Parti o braço' = I broke my arm. Braço = arm; abraço = hug.

words.example: Dói-me a perna.
words.exampleTranslation: My leg hurts.
words.proTip: Perna = leg. 'Dói-me a perna' = My leg hurts. Feminine.

words.example: Os pés estão frios.
words.exampleTranslation: My feet are cold.
words.proTip: Pé (foot) → pés (feet). Irregular! 'Os pés estão frios' = My feet are cold.

words.example: Tenho dores nas costas.
words.exampleTranslation: I have back pain.
words.proTip: Costas = back. Always plural! 'Tenho dores nas costas' = I have back pain.

words.example: Dói-me o peito.
words.exampleTranslation: My chest hurts.

words.example: Dói-me a barriga.
words.exampleTranslation: My stomach hurts.
words.proTip: Barriga = belly/stomach. Informal. 'Dói-me a barriga' = My stomach hurts. Estômago is more formal.

words.example: Cortei o dedo.
words.exampleTranslation: I cut my finger.
words.proTip: Dedo = finger or toe. 'Dedo do pé' = toe. 'Dedo da mão' = finger. Same word for both.

words.example: Tenho dores no pescoço.
words.exampleTranslation: I have neck pain.

words.example: O ombro está melhor.
words.exampleTranslation: My shoulder is better.

words.example: Machuquei o joelho.
words.exampleTranslation: I hurt my knee.

words.example: Tenho muita dor.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm in a lot of pain.
words.proTip: Dor = pain. Feminine: 'tenho muita dor.' 'Dói-me' = it hurts me — use with body parts.

words.example: Tenho uma dor de cabeça forte.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a bad headache.
words.proTip: Dor de cabeça = headache. 'Tenho uma dor de cabeça forte' = I have a bad headache.

words.example: O miúdo tem febre.
words.exampleTranslation: The child has a fever.
words.proTip: Febre = fever. 'Tenho febre' = I have a fever. Go to farmácia first — they can advise.

words.example: Estou com constipação.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a cold. (False friend: in Portuguese constipação means cold, not constipation.)
words.proTip: FALSE FRIEND! 'Constipação' = cold (illness), NOT constipation! For constipation: 'obstipação' or 'prisão de ventre.'

words.example: Apanhei uma gripe.
words.exampleTranslation: I caught the flu.
words.proTip: Gripe = flu. 'Apanhei uma gripe' = I caught the flu. Vaccination: 'vacina da gripe.'

words.example: Tenho tosse há uma semana.
words.exampleTranslation: I've had a cough for a week.
words.proTip: Tosse = cough. 'Tenho tosse' = I have a cough. Feminine.

words.example: Tenho alergia a amendoins.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm allergic to peanuts.

words.example: Preciso de uma receita médica.
words.exampleTranslation: I need a prescription.

words.example: Tomo um comprimido por dia.
words.exampleTranslation: I take one pill a day.
words.proTip: Comprimido = pill/tablet. 'Tomar um comprimido' = to take a pill. De manhã/à noite = morning/evening.

words.example: O medicamento está na farmácia.
words.exampleTranslation: The medicine is at the pharmacy.

words.example: Estou doente, não vou trabalhar.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm sick, I'm not going to work.
words.proTip: Doente = sick/ill. 'Estou doente' = I'm sick. Can also mean 'patient' (o doente).

words.example: Como de forma saudável.
words.exampleTranslation: I eat healthily.
words.proTip: Saudável = healthy. 'Vida saudável' = healthy lifestyle. Comida saudável = healthy food.

words.example: Estou muito cansado.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm very tired.
words.proTip: Cansado/cansada = tired. Agrees with speaker: men say cansado, women cansada.

words.example: Tenho uma consulta no médico às três.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a doctor's appointment at three.

words.example: Foi levado para a urgência.
words.exampleTranslation: He was taken to A&E.

words.example: Fiz análises ao sangue.
words.exampleTranslation: I had blood tests.

words.example: Tomei a vacina da gripe.
words.exampleTranslation: I had the flu vaccine.

words.example: Precisa de uma operação.
words.exampleTranslation: He needs an operation.

words.example: Dói-me aqui.
words.exampleTranslation: It hurts here.
words.proTip: 'Dói-me' = it hurts me. 'Dói-me a cabeça' = I have a headache. The 'me' is the indirect object.

words.example: Espero que melhores em breve.
words.exampleTranslation: I hope you get better soon.
words.proTip: Melhorar = to get better. 'Espero que melhores em breve' = I hope you get better soon.

words.example: O médico passou-me uma receita.
words.exampleTranslation: The doctor gave me a prescription.

words.example: Fui às urgências ontem à noite.
words.exampleTranslation: I went to A&E last night.
words.proTip: Urgências = A&E / ER. 'Fui às urgências' = I went to A&E. For emergencies, go to hospital.

words.example: Preciso de um penso rápido.
words.exampleTranslation: I need a plaster.
words.proTip: Penso = plaster/band-aid. 'Penso rápido' = sticking plaster. At the farmácia.

words.example: Tenho dor de garganta.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a sore throat.

words.example: Tenho muitas dores de costas.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a lot of backache.

words.example: Não vou trabalhar, estou doente.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm not going to work, I'm sick.
words.proTip: 'Estou doente' = I'm sick. Common excuse: 'Não vou trabalhar, estou doente.'

words.example: Dói-me aqui no braço.
words.exampleTranslation: It hurts here in my arm.

words.example: Tenho febre e dor de cabeça.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a fever and a headache.
words.proTip: 'Tenho febre' = I have a fever. Thermometer = termómetro. 38°+ is febre.

words.example: Sou alérgico a amendoins.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm allergic to peanuts.

words.example: Tens seguro de saúde?
words.exampleTranslation: Do you have health insurance?

words.example: Estou constipado, vou ficar em casa.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a cold, I'll stay at home.

words.example: A criança tem dor de barriga.
words.exampleTranslation: The child has a stomachache.

words.example: O coração dele é forte.
words.exampleTranslation: His heart is strong.

words.example: Fumar faz mal aos pulmões.
words.exampleTranslation: Smoking is bad for the lungs.

words.example: Tenho dores de estômago.
words.exampleTranslation: I have stomach pains.

words.example: Preciso de fazer análises ao sangue.
words.exampleTranslation: I need to have blood tests.

words.example: Tens a pele queimada do sol.
words.exampleTranslation: Your skin is sunburnt.

words.example: Estou a fazer uma dieta saudável.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm following a healthy diet.

words.example: Faço exercício três vezes por semana.
words.exampleTranslation: I exercise three times a week.

words.example: O bem-estar mental é muito importante.
words.exampleTranslation: Mental well-being is very important.

words.example: Às duas da manhã só a farmácia de serviço está aberta.
words.exampleTranslation: At two in the morning only the duty pharmacy is open.
words.proTip: Every pharmacy posts on its door which farmácia de serviço is open that night in the area.

words.example: Fizeram-me uma radiografia ao pulso.
words.exampleTranslation: They X-rayed my wrist.

words.example: Este medicamento pode ter efeitos secundários.
words.exampleTranslation: This medicine can have side effects.

words.example: A enfermeira mediu-me a tensão arterial.
words.exampleTranslation: The nurse took my blood pressure.
words.proTip: In everyday speech people just say «a tensão»: «Tenho a tensão alta.»

words.example: Torci o tornozelo a descer a calçada.
words.exampleTranslation: I sprained my ankle going down the cobbled street.

words.example: O meu filho partiu um braço a jogar à bola.
words.exampleTranslation: My son broke his arm playing football.
words.proTip: EP uses «partir» for breaking bones and objects; «quebrar» sounds Brazilian or very formal.

words.example: Põe esta pomada duas vezes por dia.
words.exampleTranslation: Put this ointment on twice a day.

words.example: Já recuperei da gripe, felizmente.
words.exampleTranslation: I've already recovered from the flu, luckily.

words.example: Depois da operação fiz fisioterapia dois meses.
words.exampleTranslation: After the operation I did physiotherapy for two months.

words.example: A farmacêutica recomendou-me um xarope para a tosse.
words.exampleTranslation: The pharmacist recommended a cough syrup.

words.example: A enfermeira deu-me uma injeção no braço.
words.exampleTranslation: The nurse gave me an injection in my arm.

words.example: Tens de manter a ligadura durante três dias.
words.exampleTranslation: You have to keep the bandage on for three days.

words.example: Andei seis semanas com o braço no gesso.
words.exampleTranslation: I had my arm in a cast for six weeks.

words.example: Põe o termómetro para ver se tens febre.
words.exampleTranslation: Use the thermometer to see if you have a fever.

words.example: O médico receitou-me um antibiótico para sete dias.
words.exampleTranslation: The doctor prescribed me a seven-day course of antibiotics.
words.proTip: Antibiotics need a prescription in Portugal; pharmacists won't sell them over the counter.

words.example: Na receção pedem sempre o número de utente.
words.exampleTranslation: At reception they always ask for your patient number.
words.proTip: New residents get their número de utente at the local centro de saúde; you need it for SNS appointments and prescriptions.

words.example: Dói-me a cabeça desde manhã.
words.exampleTranslation: My head has been hurting since this morning.
words.proTip: The thing that hurts is the subject: «Doem-me as costas» (my back hurts), with plural agreement.

words.example: Senti-me mal no metro e tive de sair.
words.exampleTranslation: I felt unwell on the metro and had to get off.

words.example: Caí da bicicleta, mas não me magoei.
words.exampleTranslation: I fell off my bike, but I didn't hurt myself.

words.example: Fiquei enjoado no barco para Cacilhas.
words.exampleTranslation: I got seasick on the boat to Cacilhas.

words.example: Bati na mesa e fiquei com uma nódoa negra.
words.exampleTranslation: I bumped into the table and got a bruise.

words.example: Esta picada de mosquito faz-me imensa comichão.
words.exampleTranslation: This mosquito bite is really itchy.

words.example: Que sintomas tem, além da febre?
words.exampleTranslation: What symptoms do you have, apart from the fever?

words.example: Liguei para o centro de saúde para marcar uma consulta.
words.exampleTranslation: I rang the health centre to book an appointment.

categories.title: Shopping & Money
categories.description: Shops, prices, payments, and everyday transactions

words.example: Não tenho dinheiro comigo.
words.exampleTranslation: I don't have any money on me.
words.proTip: Dinheiro = money. 'Trocar dinheiro' = exchange money. Portugal uses euros (euros).

words.example: Qual é o preço?
words.exampleTranslation: What is the price?
words.proTip: 'Qual é o preço?' = What's the price? For bargaining (rare in Portugal except at markets): 'Pode fazer melhor preço?' (Can you do a better price?)

words.example: Está barato.
words.exampleTranslation: It's cheap.
words.proTip: Barato = cheap. 'É barato' = It's cheap. Supermercados have 'preços baixos' (low prices).

words.example: Lisboa é caro.
words.exampleTranslation: Lisbon is expensive.
words.proTip: Caro = expensive. 'Lisboa está cara' = Lisbon is expensive. Renda (rent) is often 'cara.'

words.example: Quer o troco?
words.exampleTranslation: Do you want the change?
words.proTip: 'Tem troco?' = Do you have change? Small shops in Portugal sometimes struggle with large notes. 'Fique com o troco' = Keep the change.

words.example: Há desconto para estudantes.
words.exampleTranslation: There is a discount for students.
words.proTip: Desconto = discount. 'Há desconto?' = Is there a discount? 'Saldos' = sales (January, July).

words.example: Verifique o saldo da conta.
words.exampleTranslation: Check the account balance.

words.example: Há um multibanco na esquina.
words.exampleTranslation: There is an ATM on the corner.
words.proTip: Multibanco = Portuguese ATMs. You can pay bills, top up phones, buy train tickets. More than just cash — it's the national payment system.

words.example: Pago com cartão.
words.exampleTranslation: I'll pay by card.

words.example: Esqueci a carteira em casa.
words.exampleTranslation: I forgot my wallet at home.

words.example: A loja abre às nove.
words.exampleTranslation: The shop opens at nine.
words.proTip: Loja = shop. 'Loja de roupa' = clothes shop. Shops close 7–8pm, some close for lunch.

words.example: Vamos ao centro comercial.
words.exampleTranslation: We're going to the shopping centre.

words.example: Compro carne no talho.
words.exampleTranslation: I buy meat at the butcher's.

words.example: A peixaria tem peixe fresco.
words.exampleTranslation: The fishmonger has fresh fish.

words.example: Compro pão na mercearia.
words.exampleTranslation: I buy bread at the grocery shop.

words.example: Preciso de ir à sapataria.
words.exampleTranslation: I need to go to the shoe shop.

words.example: Comprei o livro na livraria.
words.exampleTranslation: I bought the book at the bookshop.

words.example: Vou comprar leite.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going to buy milk.

words.example: Eles vendem fruta no mercado.
words.exampleTranslation: They sell fruit at the market.

words.example: Quanto é para pagar?
words.exampleTranslation: How much is it to pay?

words.example: Não quero gastar muito.
words.exampleTranslation: I don't want to spend much.

words.example: Quer o recibo?
words.exampleTranslation: Do you want the receipt?

words.example: Envie a fatura por email.
words.exampleTranslation: Send the invoice by email.

words.example: Está tudo em saldos.
words.exampleTranslation: Everything is on sale.

words.example: Há uma promoção esta semana.
words.exampleTranslation: There is a promotion this week.

words.example: Tens uma moeda de um euro?
words.exampleTranslation: Do you have a one euro coin?

words.example: Só tenho notas de vinte.
words.exampleTranslation: I only have twenty euro notes.

words.example: Podes trocar-me dez euros?
words.exampleTranslation: Can you give me change for ten euros?

words.example: Quero devolver este casaco.
words.exampleTranslation: I want to return this coat.

words.example: Posso experimentar esta camisa?
words.exampleTranslation: Can I try on this shirt?

words.example: Qual é o seu tamanho?
words.exampleTranslation: What is your size?

words.example: Paga na caixa, por favor.
words.exampleTranslation: Pay at the till, please.

words.example: Precisa de um saco?
words.exampleTranslation: Do you need a bag?

words.example: Esta camisa está em oferta.
words.exampleTranslation: This shirt is on offer.

words.example: O balanço da conta está positivo.
words.exampleTranslation: The account balance is positive.

words.example: Estou a poupar para as férias.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm saving for the holidays.

words.example: A minha encomenda já chegou.
words.exampleTranslation: My order has arrived.

words.example: Encomendei um livro online.
words.exampleTranslation: I ordered a book online.

words.example: Não vendemos fiado.
words.exampleTranslation: We don't sell on credit.

words.example: Guarde o talão para devoluções.
words.exampleTranslation: Keep the receipt for returns.

words.example: Estes sapatos estão em promoção.
words.exampleTranslation: These shoes are on sale.

words.example: Preciso de abrir uma conta bancária.
words.exampleTranslation: I need to open a bank account.

words.example: Podes fazer uma transferência bancária.
words.exampleTranslation: You can do a bank transfer.

words.example: Custa cinco euros.
words.exampleTranslation: It costs five euros.

words.example: São noventa e nove cêntimos.
words.exampleTranslation: It's ninety-nine cents.

words.example: Pago com cartão de débito.
words.exampleTranslation: I pay with a debit card.

words.example: Não gosto de usar o cartão de crédito.
words.exampleTranslation: I don't like using the credit card.

words.example: Este telemóvel tem dois anos de garantia.
words.exampleTranslation: This phone has a two-year warranty.

words.example: Não cabe no orçamento este mês.
words.exampleTranslation: It doesn't fit the budget this month.

words.example: A entrada é grátis.
words.exampleTranslation: Entry is free.

words.example: Quanto custa este livro?
words.exampleTranslation: How much does this book cost?

words.example: Vou enviar uma carta para a minha mãe.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going to send a letter to my mother.

words.example: Preciso de um envelope grande.
words.exampleTranslation: I need a large envelope.

words.example: Quanto custa um selo para Inglaterra?
words.exampleTranslation: How much is a stamp to England?

words.example: Qual é o teu código postal?
words.exampleTranslation: What's your postcode?

words.example: O carteiro passa de manhã.
words.exampleTranslation: The postman comes in the morning.

words.example: Fiz um depósito no banco.
words.exampleTranslation: I made a deposit at the bank.

words.example: Preciso de fazer um levantamento.
words.exampleTranslation: I need to make a withdrawal.

words.example: Pedi um empréstimo ao banco.
words.exampleTranslation: I applied for a bank loan.

words.example: A taxa de juros está alta.
words.exampleTranslation: The interest rate is high.

words.example: Verifiquei o extrato bancário.
words.exampleTranslation: I checked the bank statement.

words.example: Tenho uma conta poupança.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a savings account.

words.example: Traga os documentos necessários.
words.exampleTranslation: Bring the necessary documents.

words.example: Tem de preencher este formulário.
words.exampleTranslation: You have to fill in this form.

words.example: Ponha a sua assinatura aqui.
words.exampleTranslation: Put your signature here.

words.example: Preciso de uma fotocópia do passaporte.
words.exampleTranslation: I need a photocopy of the passport.

words.example: O documento precisa de um carimbo.
words.exampleTranslation: The document needs a stamp.

words.example: Preciso de um NIF para abrir conta.
words.exampleTranslation: I need a tax number to open an account.

words.example: Fui às finanças tratar do NIF.
words.exampleTranslation: I went to the tax office to get my NIF.

words.example: A câmara municipal fica na praça.
words.exampleTranslation: The town hall is in the square.

words.example: Está inscrito na segurança social?
words.exampleTranslation: Are you registered with social security?

words.example: O IVA é o imposto sobre o consumo.
words.exampleTranslation: VAT is the consumption tax.

words.example: A taxa de câmbio está favorável.
words.exampleTranslation: The exchange rate is favourable.

words.example: O prazo é até sexta-feira.
words.exampleTranslation: The deadline is Friday.

words.example: Quero fazer uma reclamação.
words.exampleTranslation: I want to make a complaint.

words.example: O atendimento nesta loja é ótimo.
words.exampleTranslation: The customer service in this shop is great.

words.example: Tenho trinta dias para fazer a devolução das calças.
words.exampleTranslation: I have thirty days to return the trousers.
words.proTip: Most Portuguese chains accept returns within 15–30 days, but by law shops only have to accept them if the item is faulty — always check the policy.

words.example: Pedi o reembolso porque o produto chegou estragado.
words.exampleTranslation: I asked for a refund because the product arrived damaged.
words.proTip: You'll also see reembolso do IRS — the income tax refund Finanças pays out each summer.

words.example: A prestação da casa subiu outra vez este mês.
words.exampleTranslation: The mortgage payment went up again this month.

words.example: Pedi um orçamento ao canalizador antes de ele começar.
words.exampleTranslation: I asked the plumber for a quote before he started.
words.proTip: In Portugal orçamento means both 'budget' and a tradesman's 'quote' — always ask for one in writing before work starts.

words.example: Não gosto de desperdiçar comida nem dinheiro.
words.exampleTranslation: I don't like wasting food or money.

words.example: Este restaurante é muito em conta para o centro de Lisboa.
words.exampleTranslation: This restaurant is very reasonably priced for central Lisbon.
words.proTip: Em conta sounds more positive than barato, which can hint at low quality.

words.example: Comprei este casaco por dez euros, foi uma pechincha!
words.exampleTranslation: I bought this coat for ten euros, it was a steal!

words.example: Se pagar a pronto, fazem-lhe um desconto de cinco por cento.
words.exampleTranslation: If you pay in full upfront, they give you a five percent discount.

words.example: Comprámos o frigorífico e estamos a pagar em prestações.
words.exampleTranslation: We bought the fridge and we're paying in instalments.

words.example: Mando-te o dinheiro por MB WAY, dá-me o teu número.
words.exampleTranslation: I'll send you the money via MB WAY, give me your number.
words.proTip: MB WAY is how almost everyone in Portugal splits bills and pays friends — you send money to a phone number.

words.example: Abrimos uma conta conjunta para as despesas da casa.
words.exampleTranslation: We opened a joint account for the household expenses.

words.example: Pede um talão de troca, caso não lhe sirva.
words.exampleTranslation: Ask for an exchange slip, in case it doesn't fit him.
words.proTip: Shops in Portugal routinely offer a talão de troca for gifts — the price isn't shown on it.

words.example: Os bilhetes para o concerto já estão esgotados.
words.exampleTranslation: The concert tickets are already sold out.

words.example: Vi umas botas na montra e entrei para experimentar.
words.exampleTranslation: I saw some boots in the window and went in to try them.
words.proTip: In Brazil it's vitrine; in Portugal it's always montra.

words.example: Guardo os cêntimos no porta-moedas.
words.exampleTranslation: I keep the cents in my coin purse.

words.example: O banco cobra uma comissão de manutenção todos os meses.
words.exampleTranslation: The bank charges a maintenance fee every month.
words.proTip: Portuguese banks are notorious for comissões de manutenção — online banks and some 'contas base' avoid them.

words.example: Este mês tivemos muitas despesas com o carro.
words.exampleTranslation: This month we had a lot of expenses with the car.

words.example: Não sejas forreta, paga-me um café!
words.exampleTranslation: Don't be stingy, buy me a coffee!
words.proTip: Forreta is informal and very Portuguese; poupado is the positive version (careful with money).

words.example: Tenho de levantar dinheiro, aqui só aceitam numerário.
words.exampleTranslation: I have to withdraw cash, they only take cash here.

words.example: Finalmente paguei a dívida do cartão de crédito.
words.exampleTranslation: I finally paid off the credit card debt.

words.example: Manda-me o teu IBAN para eu fazer a transferência.
words.exampleTranslation: Send me your IBAN so I can make the transfer.
words.proTip: Portuguese IBANs start with PT50; older people may still say NIB for the same thing.

words.example: O pagamento da renda é feito até ao dia oito.
words.exampleTranslation: The rent payment is due by the eighth.

words.example: Fui ao banco depositar um cheque da minha avó.
words.exampleTranslation: I went to the bank to deposit a cheque from my grandmother.

categories.title: Nature & Animals
categories.description: Animals, plants, landscapes, and the natural world

words.example: O cão está no jardim.
words.exampleTranslation: The dog is in the garden.
words.proTip: Cão → cães (dog/dogs). Irregular plural! Very common pet. 'O cão' = the dog.

words.example: Tenho um gato preto.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a black cat.
words.proTip: Gato = cat. Gato/gatos. 'O gato está a dormir' = The cat is sleeping. Popular pets.

words.example: O pássaro canta de manhã.
words.exampleTranslation: The bird sings in the morning.
words.proTip: Pássaro = bird. Portugal has diverse birdlife. 'Ouço os pássaros' = I hear the birds.

words.example: O peixe vive no aquário.
words.exampleTranslation: The fish lives in the aquarium.
words.proTip: Peixe = fish. Same singular/plural in some contexts. Portugal eats a lot of peixe — coastal nation.

words.example: Os cavalos estão no campo.
words.exampleTranslation: The horses are in the field.

words.example: A vaca dá leite.
words.exampleTranslation: The cow gives milk.

words.example: O galo canta ao amanhecer.
words.exampleTranslation: The rooster crows at dawn.

words.example: As galinhas põem ovos.
words.exampleTranslation: The hens lay eggs.

words.example: O coelho come cenouras.
words.exampleTranslation: The rabbit eats carrots.

words.example: Uma borboleta pousou na flor.
words.exampleTranslation: A butterfly landed on the flower.

words.example: Cuidado com a abelha.
words.exampleTranslation: Watch out for the bee.

words.example: A árvore é muito alta.
words.exampleTranslation: The tree is very tall.
words.proTip: Árvore = tree. Feminine. 'Sob a árvore' = under the tree. Portuguese love their olive trees (oliveiras).

words.example: Comprei flores para a minha mãe.
words.exampleTranslation: I bought flowers for my mother.
words.proTip: Flor = flower. Feminine. 'As flores estão bonitas' = The flowers are beautiful. Portugal has stunning wildflowers.

words.example: O rio Tejo atravessa Lisboa.
words.exampleTranslation: The Tagus river crosses Lisbon.
words.proTip: Rio = river. Tejo, Douro, Mondego — Portugal's main rivers. 'À beira-rio' = by the river.

words.example: O mar está calmo hoje.
words.exampleTranslation: The sea is calm today.
words.proTip: Mar = sea. Masculine: o mar. 'Vou ao mar' = I'm going to the sea. Portugal = 800+ km of coast.

words.example: Subimos a montanha.
words.exampleTranslation: We climbed the mountain.
words.proTip: Montanha = mountain. Serra da Estrela is the highest. 'Fazer uma caminhada na montanha.'

words.example: Nadámos no lago.
words.exampleTranslation: We swam in the lake.

words.example: A floresta é densa.
words.exampleTranslation: The forest is dense.

words.example: Vivo no campo.
words.exampleTranslation: I live in the countryside.
words.proTip: Campo = countryside/field. 'Viver no campo' = to live in the countryside. Alentejo = vast campos.

words.example: O céu está azul.
words.exampleTranslation: The sky is blue.

words.example: Há muitas estrelas esta noite.
words.exampleTranslation: There are many stars tonight.

words.example: A lua está bonita.
words.exampleTranslation: The moon looks beautiful.

words.example: A terra é fértil aqui.
words.exampleTranslation: The land is fertile here.

words.example: A Madeira é uma ilha.
words.exampleTranslation: Madeira is an island.

words.example: A paisagem é deslumbrante.
words.exampleTranslation: The scenery is stunning.

words.example: O lobo ibérico está em perigo.
words.exampleTranslation: The Iberian wolf is endangered.

words.example: Vi uma raposa no campo.
words.exampleTranslation: I saw a fox in the countryside.

words.example: Há golfinhos na costa do Algarve.
words.exampleTranslation: There are dolphins on the Algarve coast.

words.example: A tartaruga caminha devagar.
words.exampleTranslation: The tortoise walks slowly.

words.example: O pastor leva as ovelhas ao monte.
words.exampleTranslation: The shepherd takes the sheep to the hills.

words.example: O porco preto alentejano é famoso.
words.exampleTranslation: The Alentejo black pig is famous.

words.example: As formigas trabalham muito.
words.exampleTranslation: Ants work a lot.

words.example: Tenho medo de aranhas.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm afraid of spiders.

words.example: Sentou-se numa pedra.
words.exampleTranslation: He sat on a rock.

words.example: A areia da praia é branca.
words.exampleTranslation: The beach sand is white.

words.example: As ondas estão grandes hoje.
words.exampleTranslation: The waves are big today.

words.example: A costa portuguesa é linda.
words.exampleTranslation: The Portuguese coast is beautiful.

words.example: A água vem de uma nascente.
words.exampleTranslation: The water comes from a spring.

words.example: A aldeia fica numa colina.
words.exampleTranslation: The village is on a hill.

words.example: O pôr do sol no Algarve é incrível.
words.exampleTranslation: The sunset in the Algarve is incredible.

words.example: Fomos dar um passeio à beira-mar.
words.exampleTranslation: We went for a walk by the sea.

words.example: Acordámos para ver o nascer do sol.
words.exampleTranslation: We woke up to see the sunrise.

words.example: Há muitos insetos no verão.
words.exampleTranslation: There are many insects in summer.

words.example: Tenho muitas plantas na varanda.
words.exampleTranslation: I have many plants on the balcony.

words.example: O jardim botânico de Lisboa é bonito.
words.exampleTranslation: The botanical garden of Lisbon is beautiful.

words.example: A Serra da Estrela tem neve no inverno.
words.exampleTranslation: The Serra da Estrela has snow in winter.

words.example: O vale do Douro é famoso pelo vinho.
words.exampleTranslation: The Douro valley is famous for wine.

words.example: As falésias do Algarve são lindas ao pôr do sol.
words.exampleTranslation: The Algarve cliffs are beautiful at sunset.

words.example: Fizemos um passeio de barco na Ria de Aveiro.
words.exampleTranslation: We took a boat trip on the Aveiro lagoon.

words.example: Moramos perto da foz do Douro, no Porto.
words.exampleTranslation: We live near the mouth of the Douro, in Porto.

words.example: O pinhal de Leiria ardeu quase todo em 2017.
words.exampleTranslation: The Leiria pine forest almost entirely burned in 2017.

words.example: No montado alentejano, os porcos pretos comem bolota.
words.exampleTranslation: In the Alentejo woodland, the black pigs eat acorns.
words.proTip: The montado is a man-made landscape of scattered cork and holm oaks; it's where porco preto and cork come from.

words.example: A minha avó tem oliveiras com mais de cem anos.
words.exampleTranslation: My grandma has olive trees over a hundred years old.

words.example: No Alentejo vês ninhos de cegonha em todo o lado.
words.exampleTranslation: In the Alentejo you see stork nests everywhere.

words.example: Cuidado com a sandes, que as gaivotas roubam tudo.
words.exampleTranslation: Watch your sandwich, the seagulls steal everything.

words.example: À noite os javalis descem à aldeia à procura de comida.
words.exampleTranslation: At night the wild boars come down to the village looking for food.

words.example: Na Serra da Lousã é fácil ver veados ao entardecer.
words.exampleTranslation: In the Lousã mountains it's easy to see deer at dusk.

words.example: É proibido pisar as dunas para proteger a vegetação.
words.exampleTranslation: Walking on the dunes is forbidden to protect the plants.

words.example: O Alentejo é uma grande planície de trigo e sobreiros.
words.exampleTranslation: The Alentejo is a huge plain of wheat and cork oaks.

words.example: Em fevereiro as amendoeiras do Algarve ficam todas em flor.
words.exampleTranslation: In February the Algarve almond trees are all in blossom.
words.proTip: Local legend says a Moorish king planted them so his Nordic wife could see «snow» in winter.

words.example: Em Trás-os-Montes há castanheiros enormes.
words.exampleTranslation: In Trás-os-Montes there are huge chestnut trees.

words.example: No verão há lagartixas em todas as paredes do quintal.
words.exampleTranslation: In summer there are little lizards on every wall in the yard.

categories.title: Emotions & Personality
categories.description: Feelings, moods, character traits, and describing people

words.example: Estou muito feliz.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm very happy.
words.proTip: Feliz = happy. 'Estou feliz' = I'm happy. Feliz aniversário! = Happy birthday!

words.example: Ela está triste.
words.exampleTranslation: She is sad.
words.proTip: Triste = sad. 'Estou triste' = I'm sad. Fado is música triste — saudade in song form.

words.example: O meu irmão está zangado.
words.exampleTranslation: My brother is angry.
words.proTip: Zangado = angry. 'Estou zangado' = I'm angry. Menos forte que 'furioso.'

words.example: Estou preocupado com o exame.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm worried about the exam.
words.proTip: Preocupado = worried. 'Estou preocupado' = I'm worried. Common state!

words.example: Fico nervoso antes de falar em público.
words.exampleTranslation: I get nervous before speaking in public.
words.proTip: Nervoso = nervous. 'Estou nervoso' = I'm nervous. Agrees: nervoso/nervosa.

words.example: Fiquei surpreso com a notícia.
words.exampleTranslation: I was surprised by the news.
words.proTip: Surpreso = surprised. 'Fiquei surpreso' = I was surprised. Surpreso/surpresa.

words.example: Os meus pais estão orgulhosos de mim.
words.exampleTranslation: My parents are proud of me.

words.example: Estou entusiasmado com a viagem.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm excited about the trip.

words.example: Mantém-te calmo.
words.exampleTranslation: Stay calm.
words.proTip: Calmo = calm. 'Fica calmo' = Stay calm. Portuguese value being calmo.

words.example: O vendedor foi muito simpático.
words.exampleTranslation: The salesperson was very friendly.
words.proTip: False friend alert! 'Simpático' does NOT mean 'sympathetic' — it means 'nice/friendly/likeable.' To say sympathetic, use 'compreensivo.' This is one of the most common mistakes English speakers make.

words.example: O empregado foi antipático.
words.exampleTranslation: The waiter was unfriendly.

words.example: Ele é tímido com estranhos.
words.exampleTranslation: He is shy with strangers.

words.example: Foste muito corajoso.
words.exampleTranslation: You were very brave.

words.example: Não sejas preguiçoso.
words.exampleTranslation: Don't be lazy.

words.example: Ela é muito trabalhadora.
words.exampleTranslation: She is very hardworking.

words.example: O aluno é inteligente.
words.exampleTranslation: The student is intelligent.

words.example: O filme é engraçado.
words.exampleTranslation: The film is funny.

words.example: Tenho saudades de ti.
words.exampleTranslation: I miss you.
words.proTip: Portugal's most famous word — there's no exact English translation. 'Tenho saudades tuas' = I miss you. It's deeper than missing; it's a bittersweet longing. Central to Portuguese culture and fado music.

words.example: O amor é importante.
words.exampleTranslation: Love is important.
words.proTip: Amor = love. 'Amor' as address = honey/darling. 'O meu amor' = my love. Central to Portuguese expression.

words.example: Tenho medo de altura.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm afraid of heights.

words.example: Não perco a esperança.
words.exampleTranslation: I don't lose hope.

words.example: Tenho confiança em ti.
words.exampleTranslation: I have confidence in you.

words.example: Preciso de paciência.
words.exampleTranslation: I need patience.

words.example: Estou frustrado com a situação.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm frustrated with the situation.

words.example: Fiquei aliviado com o resultado.
words.exampleTranslation: I was relieved with the result.

words.example: Sou muito curioso por natureza.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm very curious by nature.

words.example: A minha avó é muito generosa.
words.exampleTranslation: My grandmother is very generous.

words.example: O meu pai é teimoso.
words.exampleTranslation: My father is stubborn.

words.example: Ela é sempre honesta.
words.exampleTranslation: She is always honest.

words.example: O cão é muito carinhoso.
words.exampleTranslation: The dog is very affectionate.

words.example: A culpa não é tua.
words.exampleTranslation: It's not your fault.

words.example: Que alegria ver-te!
words.exampleTranslation: What a joy to see you!

words.example: Sentiu muita raiva.
words.exampleTranslation: He felt a lot of rage.

words.example: Que vergonha!
words.exampleTranslation: How embarrassing!

words.example: Tenho muito orgulho no meu filho.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm very proud of my son.

words.example: Estou muito cansado.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm very tired.
words.proTip: Cansado/cansada = tired. Agrees with speaker: men say cansado, women cansada.

words.example: As crianças estão entediadas.
words.exampleTranslation: The children are bored.

words.example: Fiquei assustado com o barulho.
words.exampleTranslation: I was scared by the noise.

words.example: Senti-me envergonhada.
words.exampleTranslation: I felt embarrassed.

words.example: O irmão está ciumento.
words.exampleTranslation: The brother is jealous.

words.example: Estou confuso com as instruções.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm confused by the instructions.

words.example: Fiquei surpreendido com a notícia.
words.exampleTranslation: I was surprised by the news.

words.example: Estamos animados com a viagem.
words.exampleTranslation: We're excited about the trip.

words.example: Sinto-me solitário às vezes.
words.exampleTranslation: I feel lonely sometimes.

words.example: Estou grato pela tua ajuda.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm grateful for your help.

words.example: Estou ansioso com o exame.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm anxious about the exam.

words.example: Ele está chateado contigo.
words.exampleTranslation: He's upset with you.

words.example: Ela é muito extrovertida.
words.exampleTranslation: She's very outgoing.

words.example: Ele é muito responsável.
words.exampleTranslation: He's very responsible.

words.example: A festa foi muito divertida.
words.exampleTranslation: The party was very fun.

words.example: Ela é muito criativa.
words.exampleTranslation: She's very creative.

words.example: Os portugueses são muito educados.
words.exampleTranslation: The Portuguese are very polite.

words.example: Que pessoa mal-educada!
words.exampleTranslation: What a rude person!

words.example: Estás a falar a sério?
words.exampleTranslation: Are you being serious?

words.example: Sou otimista em relação ao futuro.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm optimistic about the future.

words.example: Não sejas pessimista.
words.exampleTranslation: Don't be pessimistic.

words.example: Ela é muito madura para a idade.
words.exampleTranslation: She's very mature for her age.

words.example: Fiquei desiludido com o filme, esperava muito mais.
words.exampleTranslation: I was disappointed with the film, I expected much more.
words.proTip: For 'disappointed', desiludido is the everyday word; decepcionado is more common in Brazil.

words.example: Fiquei tão envergonhado quando me enganei no nome dela.
words.exampleTranslation: I was so embarrassed when I got her name wrong.
words.proTip: Embaraçada doesn't mean 'embarrassed' in the usual sense — use envergonhado.

words.example: O namorado dela é muito ciumento, não a deixa sair sozinha.
words.exampleTranslation: Her boyfriend is very jealous, he won't let her go out alone.

words.example: Não sejas invejoso, ela trabalhou muito para ter aquilo.
words.exampleTranslation: Don't be envious, she worked hard to get that.

words.example: Foi muito egoísta da tua parte não ajudar ninguém.
words.exampleTranslation: It was very selfish of you not to help anyone.

words.example: Ele é muito sensível, não lhe digas isso assim.
words.exampleTranslation: He's very sensitive, don't say it to him like that.
words.proTip: False friend: sensível = sensitive; 'sensible' is sensato.

words.example: O meu avô é desconfiado de tudo o que vem da internet.
words.exampleTranslation: My grandad is suspicious of everything from the internet.

words.example: Ela ficou chateada porque não lhe liguei.
words.exampleTranslation: She got upset because I didn't call her.
words.proTip: Chateado is the go-to everyday word for 'upset' or 'annoyed' in Portugal — much more common than zangado in casual speech.

words.example: Hoje não tenho vontade nenhuma de sair de casa.
words.exampleTranslation: Today I don't feel like leaving the house at all.
words.proTip: In Portugal, apetecer is even more common: «Apetece-me um gelado» = I fancy an ice cream.

words.example: Sinto falta do sol quando estou fora de Portugal.
words.exampleTranslation: I miss the sun when I'm away from Portugal.
words.proTip: Ter saudades de is warmer and more emotional; sentir falta de can be more practical — you sentir falta of your car, too.

words.english: to vent, get something off your chest
words.example: Precisava de desabafar com alguém depois daquele dia horrível.
words.exampleTranslation: I needed to vent to someone after that horrible day.

words.example: Não te preocupes, eu trato disso amanhã.
words.exampleTranslation: Don't worry, I'll deal with it tomorrow.

words.example: Arrependo-me de não ter aprendido português mais cedo.
words.exampleTranslation: I regret not learning Portuguese sooner.

words.example: Fiquei magoado com o que ele disse no jantar.
words.exampleTranslation: I was hurt by what he said at dinner.

words.example: Fico irritado quando as pessoas não respeitam a fila.
words.exampleTranslation: I get irritated when people don't respect the queue.

words.example: Fiquei muito comovido com o discurso da minha irmã.
words.exampleTranslation: I was very moved by my sister's speech.

words.example: Estou muito grato por tudo o que fizeste por mim.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm very grateful for everything you did for me.

words.example: O meu colega está sempre bem-disposto, mesmo à segunda-feira.
words.exampleTranslation: My colleague is always cheerful, even on Mondays.
words.proTip: Careful: mal-disposto usually means feeling physically queasy, not just grumpy.

words.example: Ele é tão convencido, acha que sabe tudo.
words.exampleTranslation: He's so full of himself, he thinks he knows everything.

words.example: O cão ficou assustado com o fogo de artifício.
words.exampleTranslation: The dog got scared by the fireworks.

categories.title: Colloquial & Slang
categories.description: Informal expressions, fillers, and everyday slang used in spoken European Portuguese

words.example: Eh pá, que se passa?
words.exampleTranslation: Hey dude, what's going on?

words.example: Bora sair?
words.exampleTranslation: Let's go out?
words.proTip: Bora = let's go. From 'vamos embora.' 'Bora!' = Let's go! Very informal, young people.

words.example: Tá, eu vou.
words.exampleTranslation: Okay, I'll go.
words.proTip: Tá = contraction of 'está.' 'Tá bem' = Okay. 'Tá bom' = That's fine. Very informal writing/speech.

words.example: E aí, tudo bem?
words.exampleTranslation: What's up, all good?

words.example: Tranquilo, não há problema.
words.exampleTranslation: No worries, no problem.
words.proTip: Tranquilo = cool/no problem. 'Está tranquilo' = It's all good. Laid-back response.

words.example: Tens razão, é melhor assim.
words.exampleTranslation: You're right, it's better this way.

words.example: Era tipo uma festa, sabes?
words.exampleTranslation: It was like a party, you know?

words.example: Ya, concordo contigo.
words.exampleTranslation: Yeah, I agree with you.

words.example: Aquela cena foi estranha.
words.exampleTranslation: That thing was weird.
words.proTip: Cena = thing/stuff. 'Essa cena' = that thing. 'Que cena!' = What a thing! Very informal.

words.example: Conheces aquele gajo?
words.exampleTranslation: Do you know that guy?
words.proTip: 'Gajo' and 'gaja' are very informal — like 'dude' and 'chick.' Fine with friends but avoid in formal situations. 'Aquele gajo' = That guy. Not offensive, just casual.

words.example: O concerto foi bacano.
words.exampleTranslation: The concert was cool.

words.example: Fica à vontade, estás em casa.
words.exampleTranslation: Make yourself at home.

words.example: Epá, não acredito!
words.exampleTranslation: Come on, I can't believe it!
words.proTip: Epá = hey/man/dude. Filler word. 'Epá, não acredito!' = Man, I can't believe it! Very Portuguese.

words.example: Eh meu, vamos ao café?
words.exampleTranslation: Hey bro, shall we go to the café?

words.example: Aquilo é bué fixe.
words.exampleTranslation: That's really cool.
words.proTip: Slang: 'bué' = a lot, very. 'Bué fixe!' = Super cool! Very Portuguese. Used by young people but understood by all.

words.example: Fica descansado, eu trato disso.
words.exampleTranslation: Don't worry, I'll take care of it.

words.example: Não me chateies agora.
words.exampleTranslation: Don't bother me now.

words.example: Curti bué o filme.
words.exampleTranslation: I really enjoyed the film.

words.example: Fogo, que calor!
words.exampleTranslation: Damn, it's so hot!

words.example: A malta quer ir ao cinema.
words.exampleTranslation: The group wants to go to the cinema.

words.example: Que vestido giro!
words.exampleTranslation: What a pretty dress!
words.proTip: Giro = cute/cool. 'Que giro!' = How cute! Very Portuguese. Can describe people or things.

words.example: O teu irmão é muito porreiro.
words.exampleTranslation: Your brother is really cool.
words.proTip: Porreiro = cool/great. Slightly older slang. 'Está porreiro' = It's great. Lisbon/Porto usage.

words.example: Que filme chato!
words.exampleTranslation: What a boring film!

words.example: Estou farto de esperar.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm fed up with waiting.

words.example: Estás sempre a queixar-te.
words.exampleTranslation: You're always complaining.

words.example: Levanta-te, mandrião!
words.exampleTranslation: Get up, lazybones!

words.example: Não sejas parvo.
words.exampleTranslation: Don't be silly.

words.example: Ando stressado com o trabalho.
words.exampleTranslation: I've been stressed with work.

words.example: Tenho uma ressaca terrível.
words.exampleTranslation: I have a terrible hangover.

words.example: Acho que lixei tudo.
words.exampleTranslation: I think I messed everything up.

words.example: Caramba, que bonito!
words.exampleTranslation: Wow, how beautiful!

words.example: Vamos conversar um bocado?
words.exampleTranslation: Shall we have a chat?

words.example: Espera um bocado.
words.exampleTranslation: Wait a bit.

words.example: Havia montes de gente na festa.
words.exampleTranslation: There were loads of people at the party.

words.example: Curto muito este café.
words.exampleTranslation: I really like this café.

words.example: Que seca de filme!
words.exampleTranslation: What a boring film!

words.example: Que azar! Perdi o autocarro.
words.exampleTranslation: Bad luck! I missed the bus.

words.example: Tive muita sorte no exame.
words.exampleTranslation: I was very lucky in the exam.

words.example: Estraguei o meu telemóvel.
words.exampleTranslation: I broke my phone.

words.example: Dou-me bem com os meus vizinhos.
words.exampleTranslation: I get along with my neighbours.

words.example: Os portugueses sabem sempre desenrascar-se.
words.exampleTranslation: The Portuguese always know how to get by.

words.example: Tenho muitas saudades de Portugal.
words.exampleTranslation: I really miss Portugal.

words.example: Ele está-se nas tintas para o que os outros pensam.
words.exampleTranslation: He couldn't care less what others think.
words.proTip: Informal and a bit dismissive; fine with friends, avoid at work.

words.example: Esperei por ele duas horas e fiquei a ver navios.
words.exampleTranslation: I waited two hours for him and was left high and dry.

words.example: Quando a conversa ficou chata, pus-me a andar.
words.exampleTranslation: When the conversation got boring, I took off.
words.proTip: «Põe-te a andar!» is a rude «get lost»; «pus-me a andar» about yourself is harmless.

words.example: Podes dar-me uma mão com as mudanças no sábado?
words.exampleTranslation: Can you give me a hand with the move on Saturday?

words.english: to mess up / put your foot in it
words.example: Meti água na reunião, disse o nome errado do cliente.
words.exampleTranslation: I messed up in the meeting, I said the wrong client name.

words.english: to cost an arm and a leg
words.example: As casas em Lisboa custam os olhos da cara.
words.exampleTranslation: Houses in Lisbon cost an arm and a leg.

words.example: Fizeram o casamento à grande e à francesa.
words.exampleTranslation: They had a lavish, no-expense-spared wedding.

words.portuguese: estar com a pulga atrás da orelha
words.pronunciation: shTAR kohng uh POOL-guh uh-TRAHZH duh oo-RAYL-yuh
words.example: Fiquei com a pulga atrás da orelha com aquela proposta.
words.exampleTranslation: That offer made me suspicious.

words.english: to be done for / in trouble
words.example: Se o chefe descobre, estamos feitos ao bife.
words.exampleTranslation: If the boss finds out, we're toast.

words.english: to have a nerve / be cheeky
words.example: Tens cá uma lata, chegar duas horas atrasado!
words.exampleTranslation: You've got some nerve, turning up two hours late!

words.example: – Desculpa o atraso. – Na boa, acabei de chegar.
words.exampleTranslation: – Sorry I'm late. – No worries, I just got here.

words.example: O concerto de ontem foi mesmo baril.
words.exampleTranslation: Yesterday's concert was really cool.
words.proTip: Strongly associated with Lisbon and slightly dated; younger people say «brutal» or «top».

words.example: Está sempre a dar graxa ao chefe.
words.exampleTranslation: He's always sucking up to the boss.

words.example: Não te armes em esperto, que eu vi tudo.
words.exampleTranslation: Don't try to be clever, I saw everything.

relatedWords.meaning: to act like / pretend to be

words.proTip: Very productive pattern: «armar-se em parvo», «armar-se em rico». Informal.

words.example: A vizinha passa o dia à janela a cuscar.
words.exampleTranslation: The neighbour spends all day at the window snooping.

words.english: to be confused / at a loss
words.example: Com tanta burocracia, ando completamente à nora.
words.exampleTranslation: With all this bureaucracy, I'm completely lost.

words.example: Esse exame é canja, não te preocupes.
words.exampleTranslation: That exam is a piece of cake, don't worry.

words.example: Hoje não tenho pachorra para reuniões.
words.exampleTranslation: I can't be bothered with meetings today.
words.proTip: Casual but not rude; very common in Lisbon when you're fed up.

words.example: Gastaram uma pipa de massa nas obras da casa.
words.exampleTranslation: They spent a fortune on the house renovations.

words.example: Os putos estão a jogar à bola na rua.
words.exampleTranslation: The kids are playing football in the street.
words.proTip: Perfectly normal for «kid» in Portugal, but the feminine is a swear word and in Brazil «puto» means «furious». Use «miúda» for a girl.

categories.title: Technology & Internet
categories.description: Telemóvel, ecrã, palavra-passe — devices, apps, and digital life.

words.example: Esqueci-me do portátil em casa.
words.exampleTranslation: I forgot my laptop at home.
words.proTip: In Portugal, 'portátil' is always used for laptop. Never say 'laptop' — although people will understand you.

words.example: O meu filho usa o tablet para desenhar.
words.exampleTranslation: My son uses the tablet to draw.

words.example: O rato do computador não funciona.
words.exampleTranslation: The computer mouse doesn't work.
words.proTip: Yes, it's the same word as 'mouse' the animal — 'rato.' Context makes it clear.

words.example: Onde estão os meus auscultadores?
words.exampleTranslation: Where are my headphones?
words.proTip: 'Auscultadores' is the standard European Portuguese word. 'Auriculares' is also used, especially for earbuds.

words.example: Liga a música na coluna.
words.exampleTranslation: Play the music on the speaker.
words.proTip: 'Coluna' also means 'column' or 'spine' — context tells you which. For audio: 'coluna de som' or just 'coluna.'

words.example: A câmara do telemóvel é muito boa.
words.exampleTranslation: The phone camera is very good.

words.example: O meu telemóvel ficou sem bateria.
words.exampleTranslation: My phone ran out of battery.

words.example: Tens um carregador que me emprestes?
words.exampleTranslation: Do you have a charger you can lend me?

words.example: Não tenho internet em casa.
words.exampleTranslation: I don't have internet at home.
words.proTip: In European Portuguese, 'internet' is feminine: 'a internet.' You'll hear 'a net' colloquially.

words.example: Qual é a palavra-passe do Wi-Fi?
words.exampleTranslation: What's the Wi-Fi password?

words.example: A rede está muito lenta hoje.
words.exampleTranslation: The network is very slow today.

words.example: Abre a página do restaurante.
words.exampleTranslation: Open the restaurant's page.

words.example: Encontrei um site muito útil.
words.exampleTranslation: I found a very useful website.
words.proTip: 'Site' (from English) is commonly used in PT-PT. You can also say 'sítio web' or 'página web,' but 'site' is the most common.

words.example: A ligação à internet caiu.
words.exampleTranslation: The internet connection dropped.

words.example: Preciso de descarregar a aplicação.
words.exampleTranslation: I need to download the app.
words.proTip: In European Portuguese, 'descarregar' = download and 'carregar' = upload. Never use 'baixar' — that's Brazilian Portuguese.

words.english: to upload / to charge / to load
words.example: Vou carregar as fotos para a nuvem.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going to upload the photos to the cloud.
words.proTip: 'Carregar' has multiple meanings: upload (files), charge (battery), load (a page), press (a button). Context is key.

words.example: Passo muito tempo a navegar na internet.
words.exampleTranslation: I spend a lot of time browsing the internet.

words.example: Já descarregaste a aplicação?
words.exampleTranslation: Have you already downloaded the app?
words.proTip: In European Portuguese, always say 'aplicação' — never 'aplicativo' (that's Brazilian).

words.example: Estás em alguma rede social?
words.exampleTranslation: Are you on any social media?

words.example: Vou ver o teu perfil.
words.exampleTranslation: I'm going to look at your profile.

words.example: Queres seguir a minha página?
words.exampleTranslation: Do you want to follow my page?

words.example: Podes partilhar este link comigo?
words.exampleTranslation: Can you share this link with me?
words.proTip: 'Partilhar' is European Portuguese. In Brazil they say 'compartilhar.'

words.example: Vou publicar uma foto do jantar.
